title.rendered: Fakeeh Health secures UAE accreditation for postgraduate medical training

content.rendered:
[et_pb_section fb_built=”1″ _builder_version=”4.27.5″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”][et_pb_row _builder_version=”4.27.5″ _module_preset=”default” custom_margin=”6px|auto||auto||” custom_padding=”15px|||41px||” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”][et_pb_column type=”4_4″ _builder_version=”4.27.4″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”][et_pb_text _builder_version=”4.27.4″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”]

UAE – Fakeeh Health has received Institutional Accreditation from the National Institute for Health Specialties (NIHS), becoming the first private health system in Dubai to achieve the recognition and strengthening its role in postgraduate medical education in the UAE.

Dr Mohammed Al Houqani, Secretary General of NIHS, presented the accreditation certificate to Fakeeh University Hospital (FUH).

He said the recognition demonstrated the hospital’s compliance with national standards for postgraduate medical education (PGME) and highlighted the contribution of academic hospitals to healthcare workforce development.

The accreditation covers Fakeeh Health, including FUH and its network of Fakeeh Medical Centers, and recognizes the organization as an approved institution for PGME training in the UAE.

It follows the successful accreditation of FUH’s Medical Internship Program.

NIHS is the UAE’s national authority responsible for regulating and accrediting postgraduate medical education and residency training.

Its institutional accreditation process assesses educational governance, faculty development, resident support, patient safety, clinical learning environments, quality improvement and competency-based medical education.

Expanding postgraduate medical education

The accreditation process evaluated Fakeeh Health’s educational framework, including institutional leadership, faculty engagement, resident wellbeing, assessment systems, research opportunities, simulation-based education and clinical training.

Fakeeh Health launched its postgraduate medical education programs in collaboration with the Dubai Health Authority in 2021.

Since then, it has expanded its academic portfolio through residency and internship programs, competency-based training, faculty development and simulation-enhanced learning.

Residents train across FUH and Fakeeh Medical Centers, gaining exposure to primary, secondary and tertiary care while working in patient-centred environments that emphasize teamwork, innovation and evidence-based practice.

Dr Mazen Fakeeh, Chairman of Fakeeh Health, said the organization viewed investment in healthcare professionals as essential to the future of the sector.

“Educating and mentoring the next generation of physicians is one of our greatest responsibilities, and this accreditation reflects years of commitment to building an academic environment where education, clinical excellence and innovation work together,” he said.

Commitment to physician development

Dr Mohaymen Abdelghany, Group CEO and Board Member of Fakeeh Health and CEO of FUH, said the accreditation reflected the collective efforts of the organization’s physicians, educators, faculty members and support teams.

He added that Fakeeh Health would continue expanding its academic programs, strengthening clinical training and creating opportunities for future healthcare professionals.

Dr Mazen Abou Chaaban, Designated Institutional Official, said the accreditation validated the organization’s educational governance, faculty engagement and learning culture.

He added that Fakeeh Health aimed to develop competent specialists and compassionate physicians committed to lifelong learning, professionalism and patient-centred care.

Fakeeh Health also thanked NIHS for its guidance during the accreditation process and acknowledged the contribution of its physicians, educators, administrators and support teams.

The organization plans to expand its residency and postgraduate medical education programs while strengthening academic collaborations, research and innovation across its healthcare network.

title.rendered: Aldar forms strategic partnership with PureHealth to build Health Longevity Communities in Abu Dhabi

content.rendered:
[et_pb_section fb_built=”1″ _builder_version=”4.27.5″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}”][et_pb_row _builder_version=”4.27.5″ _module_preset=”default” custom_margin=”6px|auto||auto||” custom_padding=”15px|||41px||” global_colors_info=”{}”][et_pb_column type=”4_4″ _builder_version=”4.27.4″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}”][et_pb_text _builder_version=”4.27.4″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}”]

UAE—Real estate developer Aldar and healthcare group PureHealth have formed a strategic partnership to develop health longevity-focused communities that integrate technology, healthcare, and wellness into everyday living.

The collaboration aims to redefine residential development by embedding preventive healthcare and well-being into the design of homes and neighbourhoods, while supporting the UAE’s ambition to become a global centre for health, longevity, and sustainable living.

The partnership brings together PureHealth’s expertise in healthcare and health longevity science with Aldar’s experience in developing integrated, people-centred master-planned communities.

It also aligns with national priorities, including the UAE’s National Strategy for Wellbeing 2031 and Abu Dhabi’s Longevity and Precision Medicine Declaration.

Integrating health into community design

Under the agreement, the two organisations will explore innovative ways to incorporate wellness and preventive healthcare throughout residential communities.

Their approach extends beyond healthcare facilities to include homes, public spaces, and everyday experiences that encourage healthier lifestyles and long-term wellbeing.

By combining PureHealth’s clinical expertise with Aldar’s data-driven approach to urban planning, the partners aim to transform advances in longevity science into practical and scalable solutions.

These measures are designed to improve quality of life while creating healthier and more connected communities.

Smart technologies to promote preventive care

According to Rashed AlQubaisi, Group Chief Operating Officer of PureHealth, the partnership represents an important milestone in the company’s mission to make health an integral part of daily life.

He said the initiative will leverage PureHealth’s Pura Clinic, the region’s specialised centre for precision health and health longevity science, to introduce technologies that support preventive care.

Planned features include advanced indoor air quality systems, smart beds, and intelligent mirrors capable of providing real-time, contact-free health insights.

AlQubaisi added that the collaboration demonstrates how cross-sector partnerships can accelerate innovation while advancing national objectives for population health and health longevity.

Creating wellness-centered living spaces

Jonathan Emery, Chief Executive Officer of Aldar Development, said the partnership reflects the shared belief that wellbeing should be embedded into the places where people live.

He explained that Aldar considers wellness a core principle in planning, designing, and operating its developments.

Working alongside PureHealth, the company aims to create communities that enable residents to live healthier, longer, and more connected lives while strengthening Abu Dhabi’s reputation as a global leader in sustainable, human-centred urban development.

Research and Innovation Drive Future Communities

The collaboration will also support joint research initiatives, knowledge sharing, and outcome measurement to strengthen evidence-based decision-making and foster innovation.

As the partnership progresses, Aldar and PureHealth will evaluate pilot projects across selected communities and assets to develop new approaches that combine healthcare, technology, and the built environment.

People worldwide spend up to 90% of their time indoors, making the quality of buildings a major factor in long-term health, particularly in hot climates such as the UAE.

Indoor air quality, access to safe water, natural daylight, and exposure to green spaces all contribute to healthier living environments.

Through this partnership, Aldar and PureHealth intend to design infrastructure that prioritises health longevity while creating resilient communities.

The initiative also seeks to connect healthcare with real estate to improve health outcomes, enhance residents’ quality of life, and strengthen Abu Dhabi’s position as a global hub for life sciences, innovation, and sustainable development.

title.rendered: King Abdullah Medical City adopts CardioMEMS HF system for remote heart failure monitoring

content.rendered:
[et_pb_section fb_built=”1″ _builder_version=”4.27.5″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”][et_pb_row _builder_version=”4.27.5″ _module_preset=”default” custom_margin=”6px|auto||auto||” custom_padding=”15px|||41px||” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”][et_pb_column type=”4_4″ _builder_version=”4.27.4″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”][et_pb_text _builder_version=”4.27.4″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”]

SAUDI ARABIA— King Abdullah Medical City (KAMC), a member of the Makkah Health Cluster, has introduced the CardioMEMS HF System at its Heart Health Centre, becoming one of the healthcare institutions in Saudi Arabia to adopt the globally approved technology for the remote monitoring of patients living with heart failure.

The initiative supports the Kingdom’s efforts to expand the use of smart healthcare technologies while enabling clinicians to detect signs of disease progression earlier and deliver more personalized treatment.

Advanced remote monitoring for heart failure

The CardioMEMS HF System continuously monitors pressure within the pulmonary artery, providing healthcare professionals with critical information about a patient’s cardiovascular status.

By tracking changes in pulmonary artery pressure, the system can identify early warning signs of worsening heart failure and fluid accumulation several days or even weeks before patients begin to experience noticeable symptoms.

This early detection allows cardiologists to intervene sooner by adjusting medications or other aspects of a patient’s treatment plan before the condition deteriorates.

As a result, the technology is expected to reduce emergency hospital admissions related to heart failure while improving long-term clinical outcomes and patients’ overall quality of life.

Unlike conventional monitoring methods, which often depend on patients reporting symptoms after they appear, the CardioMEMS HF System provides continuous physiological data that enables a more proactive approach to disease management.

The information generated by the system helps physicians make timely, evidence-based decisions while minimizing the risk of severe complications associated with heart failure.

Designed for patients at higher risk

According to the medical team at King Abdullah Medical City, the technology is primarily intended for patients diagnosed with Class II and Class III heart failure under the American Heart Association (AHA) classification system.

These patients remain at significant risk of disease progression despite ongoing treatment and are considered among those most likely to benefit from continuous remote monitoring.

By identifying changes in pulmonary artery pressure before symptoms worsen, clinicians can optimise treatment plans more effectively and help prevent repeated episodes of heart failure decompensation that often require hospitalisation.

Wireless implant and home-based monitoring

The CardioMEMS HF System consists of an ultra-small wireless sensor that physicians permanently implant into the pulmonary artery during a minimally invasive right-heart catheterization procedure.

The device does not require batteries or connecting wires, allowing it to function safely inside the body over the long term.

The system also includes a next-generation home monitoring unit that enables patients to record daily measurements without visiting a healthcare facility.

During the process, patients simply lie on a specially designed electronic pillow for a few minutes while the device captures pulmonary artery pressure readings.

The information is then transmitted wirelessly to the treating medical team, allowing clinicians to review the data remotely and make timely adjustments to therapy whenever necessary.

This continuous flow of clinical information supports closer follow-up between hospital visits while helping healthcare providers respond promptly to changes in a patient’s condition.

title.rendered: Dubai Investments to take full ownership of Clemenceau Medical Center Dubai in non-cash deal

content.rendered:
[et_pb_section fb_built=”1″ _builder_version=”4.27.5″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”][et_pb_row _builder_version=”4.27.5″ _module_preset=”default” custom_margin=”6px|auto||auto||” custom_padding=”15px|||41px||” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”][et_pb_column type=”4_4″ _builder_version=”4.27.4″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”][et_pb_text _builder_version=”4.27.4″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”]

UAE— Dubai Investments has agreed to acquire the remaining 80 per cent of Clemenceau Medical Center (CMC) Dubai, giving the diversified investment group full ownership of the specialist hospital.

The transaction will be completed through Dubai Investments Industries LLC, a wholly owned subsidiary, under a non-cash arrangement with the medical centre’s two other shareholders.

Khansaheb Investment LLC will transfer its 55 per cent stake, while Clemenceau Medical Company S.A.E.M.L. will sell its 25 per cent holding.

Dubai Investments currently owns 20 per cent of Clemenceau Medical Center FZ-LLC.

Once the transaction is completed, the group will hold 100 per cent of the hospital and convert it from an associate into a fully controlled subsidiary.

The company disclosed the agreement to the Dubai Financial Market but did not disclose the transaction’s value or provide details of the assets or securities that will comprise the non-cash consideration.

The deal remains subject to agreed conditions and applicable regulatory approvals.

Hospital strengthens Dubai healthcare presence

CMC Dubai operates a multidisciplinary hospital in Dubai Healthcare City, providing services in cardiology, oncology, orthopaedics, neurology, gastroenterology, women’s health, paediatrics and surgical care.

 The facility forms part of the Clemenceau Medicine International network, which originated in Beirut and has expanded across the Middle East.

The hospital also maintains an affiliation with Johns Hopkins Medicine International, supporting clinical collaboration, institutional development and healthcare quality programmes.

Dubai Investments acquired its initial 20 per cent stake in the project in 2018.

The hospital was developed at an estimated cost of AED465 million (US$126.7 million), with Khansaheb Investment holding 55 per cent and Clemenceau Medical Company owning 25 per cent.

The facility was initially planned as a 110-bed hospital and was designed to provide specialised care supported by advanced diagnostic systems, operating theatres, intensive care services and outpatient clinics.

Growing healthcare investment

The acquisition comes as Dubai’s private healthcare sector continues to attract institutional investment, driven by population growth, expanding insurance coverage, medical tourism and rising demand for complex medical services.

Meanwhile, healthcare providers are increasing capacity in areas such as oncology, cardiovascular care, fertility, rehabilitation and chronic disease management.

 Established hospitals with recognised brands and the ability to serve local and international patients have also become attractive investment targets.

For Dubai Investments, the acquisition could strengthen its control over CMC Dubai’s strategy, finances and expansion plans.

The group also holds an interest in KCH Healthcare LLC, which operates King’s College Hospital London facilities in Dubai.

Dubai Investments increased its stake in KCH Healthcare to 31.75 per cent in 2024, further expanding its exposure to the healthcare sector.

title.rendered: Cambridge Health Saudi Arabia expands licensed capacity in Al Khobar to 150 beds

content.rendered:
[et_pb_section fb_built=”1″ _builder_version=”4.27.5″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”][et_pb_row _builder_version=”4.27.5″ _module_preset=”default” custom_margin=”6px|auto||auto||” custom_padding=”15px|||41px||” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”][et_pb_column type=”4_4″ _builder_version=”4.27.4″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”][et_pb_text _builder_version=”4.27.4″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”]

UAE—Cambridge Health Saudi Arabia has secured regulatory approval to expand the licensed capacity of Cambridge Hospital Al Khobar from 100 to 150 beds, representing a 50% increase as the company continues to strengthen its specialist post-acute healthcare network across the Kingdom.

The expansion raises the group’s total licensed capacity in Saudi Arabia to 420 beds and represents another milestone in its long-term growth strategy.

Cambridge Health Saudi Arabia expects its licensed capacity to approach 500 beds once ongoing expansion projects at Cambridge Hospital Jeddah are completed and additional beds at Cambridge Hospital Dhahran receive regulatory approval.

Expanding specialist healthcare services

Since entering the Saudi market, Cambridge Health Group has invested more than SAR500 million (US$133.3 million) to establish and expand specialist post-acute healthcare services.

The investment reflects the company’s long-term commitment to supporting Saudi Arabia’s healthcare transformation under Vision 2030 while addressing the growing demand for rehabilitation, long-term care, and complex continuing care services.

The investment programme has included the establishment of Cambridge Hospital Al Khobar, as well as the opening and subsequent expansion of Cambridge Hospital Dhahran.

In addition, the company has undertaken a comprehensive refurbishment and expansion of Cambridge Hospital Jeddah, transforming it into a 200-bed specialist healthcare facility.

Construction is also underway on a further 70-bed expansion at the Jeddah hospital. The project will increase inpatient capacity while introducing new outpatient and surgical services to broaden access to specialist care.

Meanwhile, Cambridge Health Saudi Arabia plans to add more licensed beds at Cambridge Hospital Dhahran as part of its continued investment across the Kingdom.

Today, the company operates Saudi Arabia’s largest dedicated specialist post-acute healthcare network, providing integrated long-term care, rehabilitation, ventilator care, home healthcare, and outpatient services to patients across the Eastern and Western Provinces.

Leadership Reaffirms Long-Term Commitment

Khalid Gama, Chairman of Cambridge Health Saudi Arabia, described Saudi Arabia as a strategic market for Cambridge Health Group and reaffirmed the company’s commitment to investing in the Kingdom’s healthcare sector.

He noted that the group has invested more than SAR500 million (US$133.3 million) in recent years to expand specialist post-acute healthcare services, underscoring its confidence in the Saudi market and its long-term commitment to supporting patients, families, and the broader healthcare system.

Gama added that as demand for rehabilitation and long-term care continues to rise, the company will continue to invest in clinical capacity, specialist services, and healthcare infrastructure to improve access to high-quality care while supporting the objectives of Vision 2030.

Strengthening the National Care Network

Dr. Mohammed Halawani, Chief Executive Officer of Cambridge Health Saudi Arabia, said the expansion of Cambridge Hospital Al Khobar represents another significant step in strengthening the company’s specialist post-acute healthcare network across the Kingdom.

He explained that each investment has focused on expanding access to high-quality specialist care and enhancing support for patients throughout their recovery journey.

He added that the increased capacity will help the company respond more effectively to rising demand for rehabilitation and long-term care services while improving healthcare access for communities across Saudi Arabia.

title.rendered: Arabian Gulf University signs contracts to complete US$260M King Abdullah Medical City and expand campus infrastructure

content.rendered:
[et_pb_section fb_built=”1″ _builder_version=”4.27.5″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”][et_pb_row _builder_version=”4.27.5″ _module_preset=”default” custom_margin=”6px|auto||auto||” custom_padding=”15px|||41px||” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”][et_pb_column type=”4_4″ _builder_version=”4.27.4″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”][et_pb_text _builder_version=”4.27.4″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”]

BAHRAIN—The Arabian Gulf University (AGU) has signed a series of strategic contracts to accelerate completion of the US$260 million King Abdullah Bin Abdulaziz Medical City and to advance major upgrades to its academic, research, and student facilities.

The agreements were signed during a ceremony attended by senior government officials, including Bahrain’s Minister of Education, Dr Mohammed Mubarak Juma, and Saudi Fund for Development (SFD) Chief Executive Officer Sultan Al Marshad.

According to AGU, the projects form part of its long-term strategy to strengthen its academic, research, and service infrastructure while supporting innovation, high-quality education, and an enhanced university experience across the Gulf region.

King Abdullah Medical City nears completion

The flagship King Abdullah Bin Abdulaziz Medical City, located near Durrat Al Bahrain, is being developed through a grant from Saudi Arabia under the supervision of the Saudi Fund for Development.

The project covers approximately 82,000 square metres, with the first phase scheduled for completion this year.

Once operational, the medical city will house more than 280 beds and provide specialised healthcare services designed to strengthen Bahrain’s healthcare system.

AGU awarded Kanoo Information Technology the contract to deploy an integrated digital ecosystem for the medical city.

The project includes information technology infrastructure, cybersecurity, healthcare information systems, institutional platforms and digital integration solutions to ensure the facility meets international operational standards from the outset.

The university also signed an agreement with Al Salam Projects Company to supply and install furniture, interior fittings and non-medical equipment.

These installations will prepare the facility for operation while creating a modern and efficient environment for healthcare professionals and patients.

Campus and student infrastructure upgrades

Alongside the medical city, AGU signed several contracts to modernise its main campus, student housing and support facilities.

Naz Al Khaleej Company will upgrade the water distribution network at the university’s student housing complex in Zallaq.

The project includes constructing two water tanks, each with a capacity of 4,000 cubic metres, and replacing ageing pipelines and related infrastructure across approximately 20,000 square metres to improve water quality and ensure reliable long-term service.

The university will also install electronic gates and access control systems at student residences to strengthen security and improve traffic management.

The project further includes new buildings and air-conditioned waiting areas for student transport services.

Research, training and recreational facilities

To enrich campus life, Mohamed Jalal Contracting Company will renovate the AGU Club in Zallaq by upgrading existing facilities and constructing new football, volleyball, basketball and padel courts.

The project also includes the complete refurbishment of the club’s squash courts.

Meanwhile, Kontra will expand the Medical Skills and Simulation Centre by adding 24 advanced medical simulation rooms across 900 square metres, increasing the centre’s total capacity to 44 simulation rooms and strengthening clinical training programmes.

AGU has also partnered with MAR Global to modernise research laboratories at its main campus through infrastructure upgrades, new laboratory furniture, specialised equipment and improved flooring to support advanced scientific research.

In addition, Al Yousif Building Materials Company will relocate and renovate the university’s animal research facility.

The new centre will feature dedicated support services, an advanced functional layout and self-contained infrastructure designed to prevent cross-contamination between research activities while ensuring safe and humane housing for research animals.

The King Abdullah Bin Abdulaziz Medical City is expected to generate more than 1,000 jobs and strengthen Bahrain’s capacity for specialised healthcare, medical education and clinical research.

The facility is being constructed on land near Askar donated by His Majesty King Hamad and funded through a grant from the late Saudi King Abdullah bin Abdulaziz Al Saud.

content.rendered:
[et_pb_section fb_built=”1″ _builder_version=”4.27.5″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”][et_pb_row _builder_version=”4.27.5″ _module_preset=”default” custom_margin=”6px|auto||auto||” custom_padding=”15px|||41px||” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”][et_pb_column type=”4_4″ _builder_version=”4.27.4″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”][et_pb_text _builder_version=”4.27.4″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”]

BAHRAIN—Total CX, a customer experience solutions provider within the Beyon Group, has entered into a strategic partnership with Ibn Al Nafees Hospital to enhance patient engagement and operational efficiency through artificial intelligence (AI)-powered customer experience (CX) services.

The agreement reflects the two organisations’ shared ambition to combine skilled customer service professionals with advanced digital technologies to deliver faster, more responsive healthcare support.

The agreement was signed by Total CX Interim Chief Executive Officer Aseel Mattar and Ibn Al Nafees Hospital Chief Executive Officer Rahma Jaberi during a ceremony in Bahrain.

Under the partnership, Total CX will deploy dedicated CX specialists alongside AI-enabled solutions designed to strengthen the hospital’s customer engagement capabilities and streamline day-to-day operations.

Focus on smarter patient services

The companies said the initiative will improve service efficiency, accelerate response times and enhance patient satisfaction by integrating AI into customer-facing operations while retaining the expertise of trained service professionals.

Rather than replacing human interaction, the AI tools will support staff in handling enquiries more efficiently and delivering a more personalised experience for patients and visitors.

Mattar said healthcare organisations are increasingly seeking smarter ways to improve customer experience without compromising operational performance.

She noted that Total CX combines experienced customer service teams with AI-enabled capabilities to help organisations build more responsive, efficient and scalable customer operations.

According to Mattar, the company looks forward to supporting Ibn Al Nafees Hospital as it strengthens the experience it delivers to patients and customers.

Jaberi emphasised that providing an exceptional patient experience remains central to the hospital’s mission.

She said the partnership will enable the hospital to strengthen its operations by combining skilled professionals with innovative AI technologies, leading to greater efficiency, quicker responses and improved service quality.

Building on Total CX’s AI strategy

The collaboration also reinforces Total CX’s broader strategy of helping organisations modernise customer service through a blend of human expertise and AI-driven technologies.

The company, which originated in Batelco’s long-established contact centre operations and now operates as part of the Beyon Group, provides customer experience outsourcing and contact centre services across sectors including healthcare, financial services, utilities and telecommunications.

It currently manages more than three million customer interactions annually through a workforce of over 200 employees.

The hospital agreement follows several recent developments across the Beyon Group aimed at accelerating digital transformation.

In recent days, fellow Beyon subsidiary Beyon Cyber became the first Bahraini company to receive CREST Security Operations Centre certification, highlighting the group’s continued investment in advanced digital capabilities, cybersecurity, and AI-enabled enterprise services.

title.rendered: JOOTRH unveils US$37.9M Medicity Master Plan to expand regional healthcare capacity

content.rendered:
[et_pb_section fb_built=”1″ _builder_version=”4.27.5″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”][et_pb_row _builder_version=”4.27.5″ _module_preset=”default” custom_margin=”6px|auto||auto||” custom_padding=”15px|||41px||” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”][et_pb_column type=”4_4″ _builder_version=”4.27.4″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”][et_pb_text _builder_version=”4.27.4″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”]

KENYA—Jaramogi Oginga Odinga Teaching and Referral Hospital (JOOTRH) will undergo a Ksh 4.9 billion redevelopment (US$37.9M) that replaces its aging, dispersed buildings with a consolidated, modern “medicity.”

A delegation from the Ministry of Health, the African Development Bank (AfDB), and Arprim Consultants recently inspected the proposed site to assess its readiness for a potential 2,000‑bed expansion.

Master plan and phased rollout

Arprim Consultants presented a master plan and feasibility study led by Principal Architect Jared Momanyi, which sets out a phased approach to meet rising regional healthcare needs.

The plan’s first phase calls for an eight‑story, 500‑bed hospital that will house specialized medical and surgical wards, a 28‑bed Accident and Emergency complex, 20 operating theatres, a 20‑bed Intensive Care Unit (ICU), and a 20‑bed High Dependency Unit (HDU).

The initial facility will also include a renal support centre, outpatient clinics, a physical rehabilitation centre, a 15‑station dental unit, rooftop solar infrastructure, water storage, and a helipad.

Expansion and supporting infrastructure

Phase II will add 600 beds together with supporting infrastructure such as a dedicated Doctors’ Plaza and expanded clinical services, and later stages will scale capacity to 2,000 beds.

The phased strategy allows construction and service upgrades to proceed while existing care continues, thereby reducing disruption to patients and staff.

Operational challenges addressed

Many current hospital buildings date back to before 1969 and create severe operational challenges, forcing staff and patients to make lengthy walks between departments.

The consolidated design compresses the hospital footprint, thereby improving staff productivity and reducing patient movement.

In addition, the new Accident and Emergency wing will link directly to diagnostic and radiology departments, enabling immediate CT scans and faster diagnostic turnaround.

Clinical design to improve safety

Designers positioned operating theatres, diagnostic units, and critical care areas, such as the ICU and HDU, close together to reduce transit times for urgent cases, a change intended to reduce delays that can harm patient outcomes.

The layout also incorporates infection‑control strategies by streamlining patient flow and separating key clinical zones to lower the risk of hospital‑acquired infections.

Stakeholder priorities and next steps

During the site visit, Ms. Nadege Balima, an infrastructure engineer and the project’s Task Manager at AfDB, said confirming space availability, identifying JOOTRH’s priority areas, and assessing staff training needs were essential preliminary steps before breaking ground.

Dr. Hezron Omollo, Head of Infrastructure Projects and Grants Management, led the touring team and emphasized the region’s urgent need for more efficient, modern medical facilities.

Partnership and leadership

JOOTRH Chief Executive Officer Dr. Joshua Clinton Okise welcomed the Ministry of Health and the African Development Bank for their partnership, describing it as central to progressing the project from planning to implementation.

 The visiting team concluded its assessment and will use the master plan findings to guide scheduling, training, and procurement decisions ahead of construction.

title.rendered: Medcare Hospital Sharjah performs UAE’s first balloon pulmonary angioplasty

content.rendered:
[et_pb_section fb_built=”1″ _builder_version=”4.27.5″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”][et_pb_row _builder_version=”4.27.5″ _module_preset=”default” custom_margin=”6px|auto||auto||” custom_padding=”15px|||41px||” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”][et_pb_column type=”4_4″ _builder_version=”4.27.4″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”][et_pb_text _builder_version=”4.27.4″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”]

UAE—Medcare Hospital Sharjah has successfully performed the UAE’s first advanced Balloon Pulmonary Angioplasty (BPA) for pulmonary hypertension, giving new hope to patients living with Chronic Thromboembolic Pulmonary Hypertension (CTEPH).

The minimally invasive procedure was carried out on a 44-year-old woman by Dr. A.B. Gopalamurugan, Structural Interventional Cardiologist at the hospital.

It marks a significant milestone, as patients with the rare condition previously had to travel overseas for this specialised treatment.

The patient had lived with severe breathlessness for more than 11 years after chronic blood clots narrowed the arteries in her lungs and placed excessive strain on her heart.

Although she underwent open-heart surgery and later travelled to the UK for pulmonary thromboendarterectomy in 2017, residual blockages continued to limit her daily activities.

“I struggled to walk with my children, complete household chores, and even perform my duties at work,” said Mrs. Sara Al Matari.

“The surgery in the UK improved my condition, but I still needed further treatment that was not available in the UAE until now.”

Minimally invasive alternative

Dr. Gopalamurugan explained that BPA uses a catheter fitted with a tiny balloon to open narrowed or blocked pulmonary arteries through a small incision in the leg.

The procedure restores blood flow to the lungs without the need for another major operation.

He noted that the patient’s previous surgeries made another open-heart procedure highly risky. BPA therefore offered the safest and most appropriate treatment option.

The intervention was completed without complications, and doctors recorded an immediate reduction in lung pressure during the procedure.

The patient remained awake throughout, walked within 24 hours, and was discharged soon afterwards.

The multidisciplinary team included Dr. Hani Sabbour, who had managed the patient’s condition for nearly a decade, and Dr. Yogeeswari Vellore Satyanarayanan, Specialist Cardiology and Pulmonary Hypertension Unit Lead.

Their coordinated care helped identify the need for the advanced intervention and ensured timely treatment.

Expanding advanced cardiovascular care

Dr. Shanila Laiju, Group Chief Executive Officer of Medcare Hospitals and Medical Centres, said the introduction of BPA reflects the group’s commitment to delivering advanced, patient-centred care closer to home.

She added that the minimally invasive approach broadens treatment options while reducing the need for high-risk surgery.

Dr. Jishan Madathil, Chief Operating Officer of Medcare Hospitals Sharjah Cluster, said the availability of BPA in the UAE will spare many patients the burden of travelling abroad to centres in countries such as the UK and the US for specialised treatment.

He also urged people with persistent breathlessness, especially those with a history of pulmonary blood clots, to seek specialist evaluation because CTEPH is the only potentially curable form of pulmonary hypertension.

Separately, Medcare recently launched the cloud-based InterSystems TrakCare electronic medical record system at Medcare Hospital Sharjah as part of a wider digital transformation programme across its hospitals and medical centres.

The platform is designed to improve clinical decision-making, streamline operations, and enhance patient care.

title.rendered: Kenyatta National Hospital launches minimally invasive esophageal surgery protocol in Nairobi

content.rendered:
[et_pb_section fb_built=”1″ _builder_version=”4.27.5″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”][et_pb_row _builder_version=”4.27.5″ _module_preset=”default” custom_margin=”6px|auto||auto||” custom_padding=”15px|||41px||” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”][et_pb_column type=”4_4″ _builder_version=”4.27.4″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”][et_pb_text _builder_version=”4.27.4″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”]

KENYA—Kenyatta National Hospital (KNH) has successfully performed Kenya’s first Minimally Invasive Esophagectomy (MIE), marking a major milestone in the country’s ability to deliver advanced cancer surgery.

The pioneering procedure was carried out on June 30, 2026, on a 43-year-old patient diagnosed with esophageal cancer.

Before surgery, a multidisciplinary team administered chemotherapy and radiotherapy to shrink the tumor.

After reviewing the patient’s response to treatment, doctors determined that curative surgery using a minimally invasive approach offered the best chance of success.

Unlike conventional open surgery, which requires large incisions in the chest and abdomen, MIE uses several small incisions, high-definition imaging, and specialized laparoscopic instruments.

During the seven-hour procedure, surgeons removed the diseased esophagus, reshaped the stomach into a narrow tube, and connected it to the remaining upper esophagus to create a new food passage.

Multidisciplinary team delivers complex procedure

Consultant Cardiothoracic and Vascular Surgeons Dr. Joseph Mutie and Dr. Obed Makori led the operation, supported by Dr. Praxidice, Dr. Muthoni, and Dr. Yakub. Dr. Billow headed the anesthesia team with assistance from Dr. P. Chelagat, while Mr. Kitema led the nursing team alongside Mr. Onyari and Mr. Collins.

Postoperative care is being supervised by Dr. L. Ooko, with continued nursing support from Ms. P. Anampiu, Ms. B. Githinji, and Ms. G. Theuri.

The minimally invasive technique offers several advantages over traditional surgery.

Patients generally experience less blood loss, reduced pain, fewer respiratory complications, smaller scars, and faster recovery.

In this case, surgeons reported minimal blood loss and no need for a blood transfusion.

The patient spent six days in the Critical Care Unit before being transferred to the general ward.

A chest X-ray performed on the third day after surgery showed no signs of infection or other chest complications.

The patient has also begun eating small portions of soft food, indicating that the reconstructed digestive tract is functioning well.

Hospital expands advanced surgical care

Lead surgeon Dr. Joseph Mutie described the operation as a landmark achievement for Kenya’s healthcare sector.

 He said the procedure reflects the international standard of care and enables Kenyan patients to receive world-class esophageal cancer treatment without traveling abroad.

Senior Director of Clinical Services Dr. Joel Lessan said the successful outcome highlighted the value of close collaboration among surgeons, oncologists, anesthesiologists, nurses, and critical care specialists.

Chief Executive Officer Dr. Richard Lesiyampe said the achievement demonstrates KNH’s continued investment in specialist training, innovation, and advanced medical technology.

The breakthrough follows another recent milestone at KNH, where surgeons successfully removed a 4-kilogram liver tumour during a complex right hepatectomy performed through an international surgical collaboration.

A few days earlier, the hospital supported the transition of its former Othaya annex into the independent Level 6 Mwai Kibaki Referral Hospital, reflecting continued investment in specialised healthcare services and referral capacity across Kenya.

title.rendered: AUBMC partners with Philips to deploy first helium-free BlueSeal XE MRI in Lebanon

content.rendered:
[et_pb_section fb_built=”1″ _builder_version=”4.27.5″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”][et_pb_row _builder_version=”4.27.5″ _module_preset=”default” custom_margin=”6px|auto||auto||” custom_padding=”15px|||41px||” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”][et_pb_column type=”4_4″ _builder_version=”4.27.4″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”][et_pb_text _builder_version=”4.27.4″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”]

LEBANON—The American University of Beirut Medical Center (AUBMC) has installed the Middle East’s first Philips BlueSeal XE magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) system, strengthening its position in precision medicine and advanced diagnostic imaging.

The investment forms part of the hospital’s broader strategy to expand access to next-generation medical technologies despite Lebanon’s ongoing healthcare and economic challenges.

AI-powered imaging for faster diagnosis

The new MRI platform combines Philips’ BlueSeal helium-free technology with SmartSpeed Precise, an artificial intelligence-powered imaging solution that delivers scans up to three times faster while improving image sharpness by up to 80%.

It also reduces image artifacts, helping clinicians make more confident diagnoses while shortening examination times and improving patient comfort.

The system supports AI-assisted reporting and instant image-quality assessment for complex conditions, including cancer, Alzheimer’s disease and multiple sclerosis.

In addition, its sealed-helium design eliminates the need for helium refills, reducing maintenance requirements and shielding operations from global helium supply disruptions.

The launch ceremony brought together AUB President Fadlo R. Khuri, Ministry of Public Health Director General Dr. Weam Abou Hamdan, representing Health Minister Rakan Nassereldine, Dutch Ambassador Frank Mollen, Philips executives, Intermedic representatives, clinicians and government officials.

Khuri described the installation as more than a technology upgrade. He said it reflects AUBMC’s commitment to ensuring patients in Lebanon and across the region receive world-class healthcare.

Abou Hamdan added that the achievement highlights Lebanon’s ability to sustain medical innovation while advancing digital transformation through partnerships with academic healthcare institutions.

Strengthening regional diagnostic capacity

Philips Country Manager for the Levant Mohammed Saleh said the partnership demonstrates how intelligent software can help clinicians make faster decisions and improve patient care.

He noted that the helium-free system also simplifies long-term maintenance while supporting uninterrupted MRI services.

The project was completed through close collaboration between AUBMC and Philips specialists and is now undergoing final optimisation before full clinical deployment.

During the launch, attendees viewed demonstrations highlighting the scanner’s advanced imaging capabilities.

AUBMC’s Department of Diagnostic Radiology remains the largest imaging centre in Lebanon, offering advanced diagnostic and interventional services.

Alongside the BlueSeal XE MRI, the medical centre recently introduced four additional high-end medical systems and fully modernised the Suhayl M. Uthman Endoscopy Unit to expand specialised patient care.

The installation comes as Philips continues to expand its AI-enabled imaging portfolio.

In recent months, the company has highlighted the broader adoption of its BlueSeal helium-free MRI technology worldwide, with nearly 2,000 systems installed to improve sustainability, reduce operating costs, and expand access to advanced diagnostic imaging.

title.rendered: Johns Hopkins Aramco Healthcare opens  advanced rehabilitation center in Dhahran

content.rendered:
[et_pb_section fb_built=”1″ _builder_version=”4.27.5″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”][et_pb_row _builder_version=”4.27.5″ _module_preset=”default” custom_margin=”6px|auto||auto||” custom_padding=”15px|||41px||” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”][et_pb_column type=”4_4″ _builder_version=”4.27.4″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”][et_pb_text _builder_version=”4.27.4″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”]

SAUDI ARABIA — Johns Hopkins Aramco Healthcare (JHAH) has opened a new Rehabilitation Center at its Dhahran Health Center campus, expanding access to specialized rehabilitation services as demand continues to grow across Saudi Arabia.

The purpose-built facility forms part of JHAH’s Care Forward plan, a long-term strategy to strengthen clinical infrastructure, increase specialist services, and improve the patient experience.

The opening follows the recent launch of the hospital’s first-of-its-kind emergency CT system in Saudi Arabia, which is designed to speed up diagnosis and treatment for stroke and trauma patients.

The expansion comes at a time when rehabilitation services are becoming increasingly important in the Kingdom.

Stroke rates have risen steadily over the past three decades, while chronic pain affects an estimated 30% of the population, or about nine million people.

Healthcare projections also suggest Saudi Arabia will need an additional 22,000 to 24,000 long-term care and rehabilitation beds by 2030 to meet future demand.

Larger facility to serve more patients

The new center spans 2,000 square meters and significantly increases JHAH’s rehabilitation capacity.

Clinical space has doubled, while the number of treatment rooms has grown by more than 60%, rising from 25 to over 40.

These include 33 private physical therapy suites designed to improve patient comfort and privacy.

The expansion will allow more patients to receive specialized rehabilitation without compromising the quality of care.

 Annual patient visits are expected to increase from about 58,600 in 2025 to 78,200 in 2026, representing a 33.5% rise.

Dr. Howard Podolsky, Chief Executive Officer of Johns Hopkins Aramco Healthcare, said the new Rehabilitation Center represents an important milestone in the organization’s approach to patient care.

He said the dedicated facility combines advanced rehabilitation services with a purpose-built environment that expands treatment capacity while improving how patients recover.

According to Podolsky, the center will support earlier intervention, deliver more personalized treatment plans, and help patients return safely to their daily activities and work.

Advanced technology supports recovery

A multidisciplinary team of rehabilitation specialists will operate the center using a range of advanced technologies.

These include robot-assisted rehabilitation systems, a dedicated Robotics Hub, a Neuro Lab, and a Performance Lab.

The facility also houses two rehabilitation gyms alongside shockwave and magnetic therapy units.

These technologies support personalized treatment programs for patients recovering from complex orthopedic procedures, sports injuries, chronic pain, neurological conditions, and movement disorders.

Earlier this month, JHAH also announced that the Rehabilitation Center would improve patient privacy, increase treatment capacity, and enhance recovery outcomes as part of its broader Care Forward transformation programme.

title.rendered: GlobeMed Gulf collaborates with Mubadala Health Dubai to expand access to integrated healthcare services in UAE

UAE – GlobeMed Gulf has signed a strategic cooperation agreement with Mubadala Health Dubai to improve healthcare access and enhance the patient experience for insured members across the UAE.

The partnership strengthens GlobeMed Gulf’s healthcare provider network while giving eligible members easier access to Mubadala Health Dubai’s integrated medical services.

The agreement also supports GlobeMed Gulf’s broader strategy of expanding access to high-quality healthcare for its growing base of insured members.

At the same time, it connects GlobeMed’s extensive regional network of insurers, employers, and beneficiaries across the Middle East and North Africa (MENA) with one of the UAE’s leading integrated healthcare providers.

Broader access to healthcare services

Under the agreement, eligible members will have streamlined access to Mubadala Health Dubai’s wide range of healthcare services.

These include diagnostic testing, day surgery, paediatric care, rehabilitation, and preventive health services delivered through a multidisciplinary care model.

The collaboration aims to simplify the patient journey by improving coordination between insurers and healthcare providers.

It also seeks to make preventive and personalised healthcare more accessible while supporting better clinical outcomes.

Speaking during the signing ceremony, GlobeMed Gulf CEO Nada Majdalani said expanding access to quality healthcare remains central to the company’s mission.

She said the partnership with Mubadala Health Dubai represents an important step in delivering seamless access to preventive and personalised healthcare services that help improve patient outcomes while supporting healthier communities.

Safeya Al Maqtari, CEO of Dubai and Northern Emirates at M42, said the collaboration will strengthen the healthcare ecosystem by improving patient access and helping optimise healthcare costs.

She added that the agreement also supports the UAE’s ambition to reinforce its position as a leading healthcare destination in the GCC and beyond.

Building on regional growth

The partnership follows GlobeMed Gulf’s recent expansion efforts in the UAE.

Last week, the company highlighted its commitment to healthcare innovation by serving as a Platinum Sponsor at GIMIC Dubai 2026, where industry leaders discussed digital transformation, sustainable healthcare, and improved patient care.

The agreement also builds on GlobeMed Gulf’s relaunch in the UAE last year, when the company reintroduced its third-party administration (TPA) services with a stronger focus on digital health management, customer-centric insurance solutions, and round-the-clock member support.

The company now serves as part of GlobeMed Group’s regional network, which supports more than 27 million insured members across 11 MENA markets.

For Mubadala Health Dubai, the partnership aligns with its continued efforts to expand collaborations that improve patient access.

Recently, the healthcare provider also partnered with Nextcare to expand access to preventive and patient-centred healthcare services across Dubai, reflecting its strategy to strengthen healthcare delivery through insurer partnerships.

title.rendered: Royal Bahrain Hospital earns regional gold certification for patient-centered care

content.rendered:
[et_pb_section fb_built=”1″ _builder_version=”4.27.5″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”][et_pb_row _builder_version=”4.27.5″ _module_preset=”default” custom_margin=”6px|auto||auto||” custom_padding=”15px|||41px||” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”][et_pb_column type=”4_4″ _builder_version=”4.27.4″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”][et_pb_text _builder_version=”4.27.4″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”]

BAHRAIN—Royal Bahrain Hospital has received the prestigious Gold Certification in Patient-Centred Care and Patient Experience under the Arab Hospitals Federation’s Gold Initiative Certificate – 7th Edition.

The recognition highlights the hospital’s commitment to delivering high-quality, patient-focused healthcare and reinforces its standing as one of Bahrain’s leading private healthcare providers.

The award is one of the Arab healthcare sector’s most respected quality recognitions.

It honours hospitals that create exceptional patient-centred care environments while adopting innovative global practices and continuously improving the patient experience across every stage of treatment.

Recognition for Patient-First Healthcare

The certification reflects Royal Bahrain Hospital’s commitment to providing care that extends beyond medical treatment.

The hospital focuses on delivering compassionate, integrated healthcare built on respect, empathy, and clear communication.

It also encourages patients to participate actively in decisions about their treatment, creating personalised care pathways designed to improve both clinical outcomes and overall patient satisfaction.

By earning the certification, Royal Bahrain Hospital joins a select group of healthcare institutions across the Arab region recognised for placing patient experience at the centre of healthcare delivery.

The recognition also acknowledges the hospital’s efforts to build a culture where dignity, safety, and quality of care are key measures of success.

Dr. Sheriff Mohamed Sahadulla, Group Chief Executive Officer of KIMSHEALTH, said the organisation was honoured to receive the regional recognition, describing it as validation of the hospital’s long-standing “Patient First” strategy.

He noted that the achievement reflects the dedication of the hospital’s medical and administrative teams, who work together to deliver not only strong clinical outcomes but also a positive experience for patients and their families throughout their healthcare journey.

According to Dr. Sahadulla, patient experience has become a defining benchmark for healthcare excellence worldwide.

He added that KIMSHEALTH will continue investing in service improvements, innovation, advanced medical technologies, and modern clinical practices to deliver comprehensive care that meets international standards while responding to community needs

Recent Community and Healthcare Initiatives

The recognition comes during a period of continued activity for both Royal Bahrain Hospital and its parent company, KIMSHEALTH.

Earlier this week, the hospital renewed its partnership with Bahrain’s Royal Charity Organization for the third consecutive year to provide free medical services for widows and orphans, including physiotherapy, orthodontic treatment, eye care, emergency services, and other specialised healthcare.

Last week, KIMSHEALTH was also announced as the Strategic Medical Partner for the “Bahrainna.. Ahd wa Walaa” national sports festival, where it will provide medical support for participants throughout the event.

Royal Bahrain Hospital continues to strengthen its healthcare services through investments in modern medical technology, quality improvement programmes, and patient safety initiatives.

The hospital operates under the KIMSHEALTH Group, which has an extensive network of hospitals and medical centres across the Gulf region and India, with a strong focus on delivering accessible, high-quality healthcare.

title.rendered: Dr. Soliman Fakeeh Hospital conducts Saudi private sector’s first stem cell transplant

content.rendered:
[et_pb_section fb_built=”1″ _builder_version=”4.27.5″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”][et_pb_row _builder_version=”4.27.5″ _module_preset=”default” custom_margin=”6px|auto||auto||” custom_padding=”15px|||41px||” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”][et_pb_column type=”4_4″ _builder_version=”4.27.4″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”][et_pb_text _builder_version=”4.27.4″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”]

SAUDI ARABIA—Dr. Soliman Fakeeh Hospital in Jeddah has performed Saudi Arabia’s first autologous stem cell transplant in the private healthcare sector, marking a major step forward in the treatment of blood cancers.

The procedure was successfully carried out on a 55-year-old patient with multiple myeloma and signals the launch of the hospital’s new Stem Cell Transplantation and Cellular Therapy Program.

Expanding access to advanced cancer care

The successful transplant strengthens the hospital’s hematology and oncology services while expanding access to highly specialized treatments within the Kingdom.

It also allows eligible patients to receive complex stem cell therapy closer to home instead of seeking treatment abroad.

Dr. Mazen Fakeeh, President of Fakeeh Care Group, said the milestone reflects the group’s long-term strategy to expand advanced medical services across Saudi Arabia.

He noted that the achievement demonstrates the organization’s commitment to delivering world-class healthcare while supporting the Kingdom’s efforts to improve the quality of specialized medical services.

Autologous stem cell transplantation remains one of the standard treatment options for medically eligible patients with multiple myeloma.

During the procedure, doctors collect a patient’s healthy stem cells after initial treatment.

Patients then receive high-dose chemotherapy to destroy as many cancer cells as possible before the preserved stem cells are returned to the body.

This process restores bone marrow function, speeds blood cell recovery, and can extend disease control while improving quality of life.

Specialized team and multidisciplinary approach

Dr. Ahmed Alsaeed, Consultant in Hematology and Bone Marrow Transplantation at the hospital, said the successful transplant demonstrates the institution’s clinical expertise, advanced infrastructure, and ability to deliver complex therapies according to international standards.

He added that patients can now access this specialized treatment without leaving Saudi Arabia.

The Oncology Center at Dr. Soliman Fakeeh Hospital provides comprehensive cancer care, from early diagnosis and surgery to chemotherapy, immunotherapy, targeted therapy, radiation therapy, and long-term follow-up.

Specialists in medical oncology, surgical oncology, radiation oncology, pathology, nursing, nutrition, and psychological support collaborate through multidisciplinary Tumor Board meetings to develop personalized treatment plans for every patient.

The center also offers minimally invasive and robotic-assisted cancer surgery, early screening programs, rehabilitation services, and supportive care for patients and their families.

Building on recent achievements

The latest milestone comes shortly after another international recognition for the hospital.

Last week, Dr. Soliman Fakeeh Hospital became the first private hospital in Saudi Arabia to be listed among Newsweek’s World’s Top 250 Hospitals 2026.

The hospital also retained its position as the Kingdom’s highest-ranked private hospital for the fifth consecutive year, reflecting continued investment in clinical quality, patient safety, and advanced medical technologies.

[et_pb_section fb_built=”1″ _builder_version=”4.27.5″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”][et_pb_row _builder_version=”4.27.5″ _module_preset=”default” custom_margin=”6px|auto||auto||” custom_padding=”15px|||41px||” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”][et_pb_column type=”4_4″ _builder_version=”4.27.4″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”][et_pb_text _builder_version=”4.27.4″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”]

SRI LANKA—The Saudi Fund for Development (SFD) and the Government of Sri Lanka have officially inaugurated the new Faculty of Medicine at Sabaragamuwa University, marking a major step forward in the two countries’ long-standing development partnership.

The project aims to strengthen medical education while helping Sri Lanka train more healthcare professionals to meet growing national demand.

Sri Lankan Prime Minister and Minister of Higher Education, Dr. Harini Amarasuriya, attended the inauguration alongside Eng. Faisal Al Kahtani, Deputy Chief Executive Officer of the Saudi Fund for Development; senior government officials; and representatives from both countries.

The ceremony highlighted more than four decades of cooperation between Saudi Arabia and Sri Lanka in supporting infrastructure and social development.

The Faculty of Medicine was built with US$50 million in funding from the Saudi Fund for Development.

The investment has created a modern learning environment designed to expand access to medical education and improve the quality of healthcare training across the country.

The new complex features advanced medical laboratories, para-clinical teaching facilities, and a well-equipped library.

It also includes student accommodation, staff quarters, a large auditorium, and a professorial unit at Ratnapura Teaching Hospital to strengthen clinical education and research.

Together, these facilities will provide students with practical training while supporting the country’s healthcare system.

Speaking at the event, Dr. Amarasuriya praised the strong relationship between the two nations.

She said Sri Lanka values the Saudi Fund for Development’s continued contribution to higher education and its efforts to create more opportunities for future generations of medical students.

Eng. Al Kahtani described the project as an investment in people, knowledge, and opportunity rather than simply a new academic building.

He noted that the Saudi Fund for Development has partnered with Sri Lanka for more than 40 years to improve lives through sustainable development projects in key sectors.

Long-standing partnership continues

The new Faculty of Medicine is the latest addition to a broad portfolio of Saudi-funded projects in Sri Lanka.

Since 1981, the Saudi Fund for Development has financed initiatives in education, healthcare, water, transport, and energy.

Through 15 development loans covering 12 projects, the Fund has committed approximately US$422.7 million to support the country’s social and economic development.

The opening comes just days after Sri Lankan officials highlighted the project’s wider impact on regional development.

The new medical faculty spans about 20 acres and is expected to accommodate hundreds of students while expanding clinical training capacity in the Sabaragamuwa Province.

Officials also noted that the facility will help decentralize medical education beyond the country’s traditional university centres and address future shortages of healthcare professionals.

content.rendered:
[et_pb_section fb_built=”1″ _builder_version=”4.27.5″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”][et_pb_row _builder_version=”4.27.5″ _module_preset=”default” custom_margin=”6px|auto||auto||” custom_padding=”15px|||41px||” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”][et_pb_column type=”4_4″ _builder_version=”4.27.4″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”][et_pb_text _builder_version=”4.27.4″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”]

SOUTH AFRICA—Johann Rupert’s investment company, Remgro, has completed its acquisition of full ownership of Mediclinic Holdings’ Southern African business after finalising a deal worth R15.56 billion (US$947 million).

The transaction marks the end of a long-standing joint ownership arrangement with Luxembourg-based Investment Holding Limited (IHL), which previously shared control of the private hospital group.

Remgro confirmed on July 1, 2026, that all regulatory and commercial conditions had been met, allowing the transaction to close.

The deal, first announced in December 2025, also received approval from South Africa’s Competition Tribunal in June after clearing regulatory reviews in both South Africa and Europe.

Ownership split completed

Before the restructuring, Remgro and IHL each owned a 50% stake in Mediclinic Holdings.

Under the new arrangement, Remgro now owns 100% of Mediclinic’s Southern African operations through Mediclinic International, while IHL has taken full ownership of the Swiss-based Hirslanden Group.

The separation simplifies the group’s ownership structure and allows each shareholder to focus on its core market.

Remgro said the new structure will enable faster decision-making, stronger regional partnerships, and strategies tailored to local healthcare needs.

The company added that both shareholders remain committed to long-term investment in private healthcare despite now operating independently.

The final purchase price was slightly lower than the R15.61 billion (US$950 million) announced last year due to agreed adjustments for leakage and accruals between signing and completion.

Remgro paid R15.56 billion (US$947 million), whereas IHL paid R17.74 billion (US$1.08 billion) for the Hirslanden business.

As part of the implementation, Remgro also received an additional US$130 million cash payment to equalise the value of the exchanged assets.

Expanding healthcare footprint

The acquisition gives Remgro full control of one of Southern Africa’s largest private healthcare networks, which includes about 50 hospitals, day clinics and specialised healthcare facilities across South Africa, Namibia and Mauritius.

 The hospitals primarily serve privately insured patients and remain a major provider of specialist medical services in the region.

The transaction also follows a strong year for Mediclinic.

Recent results showed the healthcare group’s adjusted revenue grew by 11% to US$5.36 billion, with a 45% increase in adjusted earnings for the fiscal year ending March 2026, driven by higher patient volumes and better operational results.

For Remgro, the acquisition strengthens a portfolio that spans healthcare, banking, insurance, consumer goods and media.

Rupert, whose family controls Remgro through Compagnie Financière Rupert, has consistently identified private healthcare as a strategic long-term investment, particularly as demand for quality medical services continues to grow across Southern Africa.

title.rendered: Mwai Kibaki Referral Hospital gains full autonomy from Kenyatta National Hospital

content.rendered:
[et_pb_section fb_built=”1″ _builder_version=”4.27.5″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}”][et_pb_row _builder_version=”4.27.5″ _module_preset=”default” custom_margin=”6px|auto||auto||” custom_padding=”15px|||41px||” global_colors_info=”{}”][et_pb_column type=”4_4″ _builder_version=”4.27.4″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}”][et_pb_text _builder_version=”4.27.4″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}”]

KENYA—The Kenyan government has officially transferred the management of Mwai Kibaki Referral Hospital (MKRH) from Kenyatta National Hospital (KNH), marking a major step in strengthening the country’s national referral healthcare system.

The handover ceremony, held in Othaya, Nyeri County, was presided over by Principal Secretary for Medical Services, Dr. Ouma Oluga.

It formally transformed the hospital from a KNH annex into an autonomous State Corporation and a fully operational National Referral Hospital.

The move is expected to expand access to specialized healthcare services while easing pressure on other national referral facilities.

Transition to Independent Management

Speaking during the event, Dr. Oluga said the transition demonstrates the government’s commitment to improving access to quality specialized healthcare, strengthening institutional accountability, and delivering better health outcomes for Kenyans.

He added that granting the hospital operational independence will bring advanced medical services closer to communities and improve the country’s ability to manage the growing burden of non-communicable diseases.

The Principal Secretary noted that the hospital became an autonomous State Corporation through Legal Notice No. 148 of 2024.

The new status gives MKRH its own Board of Directors, an approved organizational structure, and direct funding from the National Exchequer.

To ensure a smooth transition, the State Department for Medical Services established a Technical Transition Committee to oversee the transfer of staff, assets, liabilities, functions, and operational responsibilities from KNH.

Dr. Oluga also reaffirmed the government’s commitment to supporting the hospital until it achieves full operational independence and delivers its mandate as a national referral institution.

Strategic Plan and Infrastructure Expansion

During the ceremony, Dr. Oluga launched the Mwai Kibaki Referral Hospital Strategic Plan 2025–2030, which outlines the hospital’s priorities in specialized healthcare, medical education, research, and institutional performance.

The strategy aligns with the Kenya Health Policy 2014–2030, the Bottom-Up Economic Transformation Agenda (BETA), Kenya Vision 2030, and the Fourth Medium-Term Plan.

He also highlighted ongoing infrastructure projects, including the construction of the Mwai Kibaki Tower.

The facility will house specialized medical and surgical units, advanced diagnostic services, critical care facilities, and modern training and research infrastructure.

According to Dr. Oluga, the expansion will improve access to advanced healthcare while positioning the hospital as a regional centre of excellence.

Recent Government Investments

The handover comes only months after the government formally elevated the hospital to an independent Level 6 national referral facility and announced additional investments to strengthen its capacity.

Earlier this year, President William Ruto announced that the government had set aside KSh1 billion (US$7.7 million) for modern medical equipment.

He also confirmed plans to expand the hospital’s infrastructure to better serve Nyeri County and neighbouring regions.

The event was attended by members of the Ministry of Health Technical Transition Committee, chaired by James Ntabo; Mwai Kibaki Referral Hospital Board Chair Lt. Gen. (Rtd.) Robert Kibochi; KNH Board Chair Dr. Abbas Gullet; Acting MKRH CEO Dr. Peter Muiruri; Acting KNH CEO Dr. Richard Lesiyampe; National Assembly Health Committee representative Duncan Mathenge; Othaya MP Wambugu Wainaina; officials from Nyeri County government; Ministry of Health representatives; hospital staff; and local leaders.

QATAR – Hamad Medical Corporation (HMC) has signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with Boehringer Ingelheim to strengthen clinical research, healthcare innovation, workforce development, and patient outcomes across Qatar.

The agreement supports the country’s broader efforts to build a more research-driven healthcare system while expanding access to cutting-edge medical advances.

Under the partnership, the two organizations will work together to enhance HMC’s Clinical Trials Unit (CTU), strengthen research expertise, and develop initiatives that support the continued growth of Qatar’s healthcare sector.

The collaboration is expected to reinforce HMC’s position as a leading center for medical research and innovation in the region.

Improving clinical trial infrastructure will also help attract more international studies to Qatar, giving local researchers greater opportunities to participate in global scientific research while increasing patients’ access to emerging therapies.

Researchers will gain broader exposure to new technologies, treatment approaches, and scientific developments, enabling them to identify future research priorities that better address the country’s evolving healthcare needs.

Building expertise in Health Technology Assessment

A major component of the agreement focuses on strengthening Health Technology Assessment (HTA) at HMC through capacity-building and infrastructure development.

The initiative will equip healthcare professionals with the skills to assess the clinical, economic, societal, and patient impacts of medicines, medical devices, and digital health technologies.

In turn, these assessments will support evidence-based decisions and improve the efficient use of healthcare resources.

Ali Al Janahi, Assistant Managing Director of HMC, said the agreement marks an important milestone in strengthening Qatar’s clinical research ecosystem.

He noted that expanding clinical trials and research capabilities will support the country’s ambition to deliver world-class, value-based healthcare while improving patient outcomes and building a more sustainable health system.

Dr. Anas Ahmad Hamad, Deputy Chief of Drug Supply at HMC and Lead of the National HTA and Innovation Regulation Program under the National Health Strategy 2024–2030, said the partnership will strengthen Qatar’s HTA ecosystem by building local expertise and establishing sustainable assessment capabilities.

He added that collaboration with industry partners will accelerate responsible access to healthcare innovations while supporting evidence-based policymaking.

Supporting Qatar’s healthcare ambitions

Derek O’Leary, Regional Managing Director for India, the Middle East, Türkiye and Africa at Boehringer Ingelheim, said meaningful healthcare progress depends on strong partnerships that translate scientific discoveries into better patient outcomes.

He added that the collaboration reflects both organizations’ commitment to advancing research capabilities and supporting Qatar’s long-term healthcare goals.

Abdallah Hamed, General Manager and Head of Human Pharma for Saudi Arabia, the Gulf, and East Africa (SAGEA), said the partnership aligns with Qatar National Vision 2030 by investing in innovation, research, and people.

He noted that closer collaboration between healthcare providers and industry is essential to ensure scientific breakthroughs reach patients more quickly through improved clinical practice and broader access to innovative treatments.

The Qatar agreement follows another regional collaboration announced only days earlier, when Boehringer Ingelheim partnered with Abu Dhabi’s Department of Health to advance precision medicine research using genomics and biobank data.

Earlier in June, HMC also launched a joint research funding initiative with Qatar University to support locally driven health research, reinforcing its broader strategy of strengthening research, innovation, and specialized clinical services across the country.
