INDIA—Aster DM Quality Care has officially begun operations following the completion of the merger between Aster DM Healthcare and Quality Care India Limited (QCIL), creating one of India’s largest integrated healthcare providers.

The newly formed organization brings together four established healthcare brands including Aster DM, CARE Hospitals, Evercare and KIMSHEALTH, under a single platform focused on expanding access to advanced and affordable medical care across the country.

The merger follows the completion of regulatory approvals and the successful integration process announced in recent days.

The combined company will continue under the leadership of Executive Chairman Dr. Azad Moopen, while Varun Khanna has assumed the role of Managing Director and Group Chief Executive Officer.

Together, they will oversee the integration of clinical services, technology platforms and operations across the enlarged healthcare network.

Expanding specialist care beyond major cities

With a strong presence across South and Central India, Aster DM Quality Care aims to strengthen healthcare delivery in fast-growing tier 2 and tier 3 cities, where access to specialist treatment remains limited.

The organization plans to bring advanced medical services closer to patients by expanding centres of excellence, investing in modern technologies and increasing specialist care outside metropolitan areas.

Dr. Moopen described the merger as a defining milestone that unites two organizations with shared values, clinical excellence and a common commitment to patient care.

He said the integration creates a stronger and more resilient institution that is better equipped to meet India’s evolving healthcare needs.

Khanna added that the immediate priority is a seamless integration that maintains uninterrupted patient care while combining systems, capabilities and best practices across the network.

He noted that patients, clinicians, employees and partners will remain at the centre of every decision as the organization adopts more digitally enabled healthcare solutions and continues to improve clinical outcomes.

Technology investments and future growth

The merged platform expects to generate combined effect in clinical collaboration, procurement, digital health, operational efficiency and technology adoption.

Physicians across the network will increasingly work together through shared treatment protocols, multidisciplinary case discussions and centres of excellence, allowing patients to benefit from broader expertise while receiving consistent standards of care.

Aster DM Quality Care now operates 39 hospitals in 28 cities with more than 10,600 beds.

The network serves patients in emerging healthcare hubs, including Nagpur, Aurangabad, Vijayawada, Guntur, Bhubaneswar, Raipur, Nagercoil, Kolhapur, Kannur, Kasaragod and Kottakkal, reducing the need for patients to travel to larger cities for complex treatment.

The company also plans to expand investments in advanced medical technologies, including Gamma Knife systems, stereotactic radiosurgery platforms such as ZAP, 10 robotic surgical systems and 12 additional LINAC-based radiation therapy units to improve access to cancer care in underserved regions.

Over the next few years, Aster DM Quality Care expects to increase its capacity to more than 15,000 beds while supporting a workforce of over 45,000 healthcare professionals.

The expansion is also expected to create thousands of new employment opportunities for doctors, nurses, allied health professionals and support staff as the network continues to grow across India.

title.rendered: Mayo Clinic discovers hormone replacement improves tirzepatide obesity treatment

content.rendered:
[et_pb_section fb_built=”1″ _builder_version=”4.27.5″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”][et_pb_row _builder_version=”4.27.5″ _module_preset=”default” custom_margin=”6px|auto||auto||” custom_padding=”15px|||41px||” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”][et_pb_column type=”4_4″ _builder_version=”4.27.4″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”][et_pb_text _builder_version=”4.27.4″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”]

UAE—Postmenopausal women receiving menopausal hormone therapy alongside tirzepatide may achieve substantially greater weight loss than those using the obesity medication alone, according to a new study led by Mayo Clinic.

The findings, published in The Lancet Obstetrics, Gynaecology & Women’s Health, suggest that combining the two treatments could offer a more effective approach to managing obesity and reducing cardiometabolic risk in women after menopause.

Greater weight loss after menopause

Researchers found that postmenopausal women taking hormone therapy while receiving tirzepatide lost approximately 35% more weight than women treated with tirzepatide alone.

Tirzepatide is approved by the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) to treat overweight and obesity and has become one of the leading medicines in the growing class of GLP-1-based weight-loss therapies.

Menopause often accelerates age-related weight gain because declining estrogen levels alter metabolism, body fat distribution, and appetite regulation.

These hormonal changes also increase the risk of cardiovascular disease, type 2 diabetes, and other obesity-related conditions, making effective weight management particularly important for women during this stage of life.

Regina Castaneda, M.D., the study’s first author and a postdoctoral research fellow at Mayo Clinic, said the findings could help clinicians develop more personalised strategies for reducing cardiometabolic risk in postmenopausal women

Study examined real-world patients

The research team reviewed medical records from 120 adults with overweight or obesity who received tirzepatide for at least 12 months.

Investigators compared women who used menopausal hormone therapy with similar patients who received tirzepatide without hormone therapy.

Hormone therapy remains the most effective first-line treatment for common menopausal symptoms such as hot flashes and night sweats, which affect up to three-quarters of postmenopausal women.

Earlier studies had already suggested that hormone therapy could enhance weight loss in women treated with semaglutide, another GLP-1-based medication.

However, this is the first study to investigate a similar relationship with tirzepatide.

Researchers call for randomized trials

Despite the encouraging results, the researchers emphasised that the study was observational rather than a randomised clinical trial.

Maria Daniela Hurtado Andrade, M.D., Ph.D., senior author and endocrinologist at Mayo Clinic, noted that the findings demonstrate an association rather than proof that hormone therapy directly caused the additional weight loss.

Women receiving hormone therapy may already have adopted healthier lifestyles or experienced improved sleep and quality of life after relief from menopausal symptoms, making it easier to maintain healthy eating habits and regular physical activity.

The researchers also pointed to preclinical evidence suggesting that estrogen may strengthen the appetite-suppressing effects of GLP-1 medicines, providing a possible biological explanation for the observed benefit.

They now plan to launch a randomised clinical trial to determine whether combining hormone therapy with tirzepatide improves not only weight loss but also broader cardiometabolic outcomes, including cardiovascular health and metabolic risk factors.

Mayo Clinic advances GLP-1 research

The latest findings add to Mayo Clinic’s expanding research on GLP-1 therapies.

Recently, Mayo Clinic researchers indicated that the links between GLP-1 medicines and thyroid cancer might mainly result from increased medical monitoring rather than a direct causative effect.

This provides additional reassurance regarding the long-term safety of these medications, which are being prescribed more frequently.

SAUDI ARABIA—Saudi German Hospital Dammam has earned the prestigious Magnet Recognition from the American Nurses Credentialing Center (ANCC), marking a major milestone for both the hospital and its parent network, Saudi German Health.

The achievement reinforces the group’s commitment to nursing excellence, high-quality patient care, and internationally recognised clinical standards.

The hospital is the first private healthcare facility in Dammam, the capital of Saudi Arabia’s Eastern Province, to receive the designation.

It also becomes the fourth hospital within the Saudi German Health network to achieve Magnet Recognition outside the United States, further expanding the group’s portfolio of internationally accredited facilities.

Magnet Recognition is widely regarded as the highest international benchmark for nursing excellence.

The ANCC awards the designation to hospitals that demonstrate outstanding nursing leadership, innovation, professional practice, patient outcomes, and quality improvement.

For patients, the recognition reflects a healthcare environment where nurses receive strong institutional support to deliver safe, compassionate, and patient-centred care.

Expanding a network of magnet hospitals

The latest recognition strengthens Saudi German Health’s position as a regional leader in nursing excellence.

With Dammam joining its list of Magnet-designated facilities, the healthcare group now operates four Magnet-recognized hospitals, making it the only healthcare system outside the United States to reach this milestone.

Within the network, Saudi German Hospital Dammam is now the first and only private hospital in the Eastern Province’s capital to receive Magnet Recognition.

Saudi German Hospital Aseer remains the first and only hospital in Saudi Arabia’s Southern Region with the designation, while Saudi German Hospital Riyadh was the first private hospital in the capital to earn the recognition.

Meanwhile, Saudi German Hospital Jeddah became the first hospital outside the United States to receive the even higher Magnet Recognition with Distinction, placing it among the world’s top-performing hospitals for nursing excellence.

Continued focus on international standards

The recognition reflects Saudi German Health’s broader strategy of aligning its services with leading international healthcare standards while advancing its “Caring Like Family” philosophy.

The group continues to invest in nursing leadership, staff development, and quality improvement programmes to enhance patient outcomes across its hospitals.

The announcement also follows a series of recent achievements for Saudi German Health.

 Earlier this year, the organisation was recognised among TIME and Statista’s Arabia Growth Leaders 2026, highlighting its continued expansion across the region.

The group also recently launched operations at a new outpatient clinic complex in Riyadh as part of its ongoing efforts to improve access to specialised healthcare services throughout Saudi Arabia.

title.rendered: Aster DM Healthcare expands robotic rehabilitation network with new Sohar facility

OMAN—Aster Al Raffah Hospitals & Clinics, part of Aster DM Healthcare, has expanded access to advanced rehabilitation services in Oman with the opening of its second Aster Al Raffah Walk Again Advanced Robotic Rehabilitation Centre in Sohar.

The new facility builds on the success of the flagship centre in Muscat and brings specialised robotic rehabilitation closer to patients in northern Oman, where demand for neurological and musculoskeletal care continues to grow.

Advanced rehabilitation reaches northern Oman

The Sohar centre was inaugurated under the patronage of His Excellency Dr. Ahmed bin Salim Al-Mandhari, Undersecretary for Planning and Health Regulation at the Ministry of Health, alongside His Excellency Mohammed bin Sulaiman Al Kindi, Governor of Al Batinah North.

Designed as one of the region’s most advanced rehabilitation facilities, the centre combines artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled robotic systems with evidence-based rehabilitation programmes to help patients recover mobility, independence, and quality of life.

Its technology portfolio includes Cyberdyne HAL, Recoverix Pro, Hand of Hope, Syrebo, Luna EMG, Vibramoov, Tymo, Pablo, VitalStim, repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS), and other advanced rehabilitation platforms that deliver personalised therapy while tracking patient progress in real time.

These systems support repetitive, precision-guided therapy that promotes neuroplasticity and helps patients regain movement after neurological injuries or disease.

Comprehensive care for neurological conditions

The centre will treat patients with a broad range of conditions, including stroke, spinal cord injuries, traumatic brain injuries, multiple sclerosis, cerebral palsy, autism spectrum disorder, muscular dystrophy, motor neuron disease, movement disorders, Alzheimer’s disease, dementia, ataxia, and dystonia.

In addition, multidisciplinary teams will provide integrated care across neurology, spine, sports medicine, and mental wellbeing.

Clinical operations will be led by Dr. Vivek Joseph, Senior Consultant Neurosurgeon and Medical Director, together with Dr. Jaikishen Agiwal, Chief Operating Officer.

Speaking during the inauguration, Dr. Al-Mandhari said the expansion reflects Oman’s commitment to improving healthcare accessibility by bringing advanced rehabilitation technologies beyond Muscat.

Governor Al Kindi added that the new centre strengthens access to specialised healthcare in Al Batinah North while supporting better patient outcomes through innovation.

Supporting Oman’s healthcare ambitions

Dr. Azad Moopen, Founder Chairman of Aster DM Healthcare, said the Sohar expansion reinforces the group’s commitment to making world-class rehabilitation available throughout Oman.

He noted that the facility also supports the “Treat in Oman” initiative by reducing the need for patients to travel overseas for advanced treatment.

Alisha Moopen, Managing Director and Group CEO, said the new centre combines compassionate care with advanced technology to deliver cutting-edge neuro-rehabilitation closer to patients’ homes.

Meanwhile, Dr. Sachin Kandhari, CEO of Walk Again India, said the collaboration brings globally recognised robotic rehabilitation systems and evidence-based clinical protocols to Oman.

Sohar was selected because it accounts for nearly 30% of patient referrals from northern Oman.

Its existing Aster Al Raffah Hospital also enables seamless coordination between acute hospital care and long-term rehabilitation.

The expansion comes as Aster DM Healthcare continues to invest in advanced medical technologies across the Gulf.

Earlier this year, the company announced plans to establish a similar robotic rehabilitation centre in Dubai, modelled on the success of its facilities in Oman, and to expand its investments in specialised healthcare services across the region.

title.rendered: M42’s IROS partners with Halia Therapeutics to launch first Alzheimer’s prevention trial in UAE

content.rendered:
[et_pb_section fb_built=”1″ _builder_version=”4.27.5″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”][et_pb_row _builder_version=”4.27.5″ _module_preset=”default” custom_margin=”6px|auto||auto||” custom_padding=”15px|||41px||” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”][et_pb_column type=”4_4″ _builder_version=”4.27.4″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”][et_pb_text _builder_version=”4.27.4″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”]

UAE—M42’s Insights Research Organisation and Solutions (IROS), in partnership with the Department of Health – Abu Dhabi (DoH) and US clinical-stage biotechnology company Halia Therapeutics has launched the UAE’s first genomics-driven clinical trial aimed at preventing Alzheimer’s disease.

The initiative marks a significant milestone in translating data from the Emirati Genome Programme (EGP) into real-world clinical care while strengthening Abu Dhabi’s position as a regional hub for precision medicine.

Alzheimer’s disease affects more than 55 million people worldwide, and that figure is projected to nearly triple by 2050.

Against this backdrop, the new study seeks to identify people who may be at high genetic risk before symptoms develop, creating opportunities for earlier intervention and a stronger focus on disease prevention.

Harnessing genomics for early intervention

The trial will analyze population-scale genomic data generated through the Emirati Genome Programme to identify eligible participants.

Following eligibility screening and genetic counselling, researchers will evaluate HT-4253, Halia Therapeutics’ investigational therapy, in symptom-free individuals who carry the APOE4 gene variant, one of the strongest genetic risk factors for late-onset Alzheimer’s disease.

The Department of Health – Abu Dhabi will lead targeted outreach by sending text messages to eligible individuals to participate in the screening process.

The department is also providing regulatory oversight to ensure that genomic data are used responsibly and in full compliance with patient privacy and data protection regulations.

Dr. Noura Al Ghaithi, Undersecretary of the Department of Health – Abu Dhabi, said the Emirati Genome Programme has become a strategic national asset that is transforming how diseases are understood, prevented, and treated.

She noted that integrating genomic information into clinical research enables earlier risk detection, accelerates diagnosis, and supports the development of more personalized preventive and therapeutic approaches.

She added that the programme also improves the representation of Middle Eastern populations in global genomics research, helping expand scientific understanding of disease across diverse populations.

Building a precision medicine ecosystem

Albarah El-Khani, Chief Operating Officer of Integrated Health Solutions at M42, stated that integrating a major national genomic dataset with Halia Therapeutics’ experimental therapy and M42’s clinical research capabilities allows researchers to identify APOE4 carriers on a large scale, especially within a group that has traditionally been underrepresented in global research.

David Kavanagh, Interim General Manager of IROS, described the study as the clinical translation of more than a decade of genomic investment in the UAE.

He said IROS was established to deliver biomarker-driven, prevention-focused clinical trials that convert genomic discoveries into improved health outcomes.

Dave Bearss, President, Chief Executive Officer and Co-Founder of Halia Therapeutics, said the company’s drug discovery strategy focuses on understanding why some genetically high-risk individuals remain healthy.

He explained that the Emirati Genome Programme provides an ideal platform for testing preventive therapies before disease develops, adding that this vision influenced Halia’s decision to establish a presence in Abu Dhabi.

Recent expansion strengthens M42’s research ambitions

The launch comes as M42 continues expanding its life sciences portfolio. In recent days, the company announced a strategic partnership with Juvenescence to accelerate AI-enabled drug discovery for age-related diseases and invested in advancing longevity research.

M42 has also unveiled new partnerships to expand precision oncology clinical trials and introduce the Middle East’s first heavy-ion cancer therapy facility, reinforcing Abu Dhabi’s ambitions to become a global centre for genomics, biotechnology, and next-generation clinical research.

title.rendered: Abu Dhabi breaks ground on SRH expansion to create UAE’s largest rehabilitation hospital

content.rendered:
[et_pb_section fb_built=”1″ _builder_version=”4.27.5″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”][et_pb_row _builder_version=”4.27.5″ _module_preset=”default” custom_margin=”6px|auto||auto||” custom_padding=”15px|||41px||” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”][et_pb_column type=”4_4″ _builder_version=”4.27.4″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”][et_pb_text _builder_version=”4.27.4″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”]

UAE—Specialized Rehabilitation Hospital (SRH), part of Capital Health, has begun construction of a major expansion in Abu Dhabi that will significantly strengthen rehabilitation and specialty healthcare services across the UAE.

The new development marks the hospital’s next phase of growth and is expected to transform SRH into the country’s largest integrated rehabilitation hospital when it becomes operational by the end of 2028.

The groundbreaking ceremony gathered senior officials from government and healthcare sectors, such as Dr. Fayeza Saif Nasir Alyafe, Executive Director of the Healthcare Quality Sector at the Department of Health – Abu Dhabi; Khalifa Al Mazrouei, Group Chief Investment Officer of Abu Dhabi Capital Group (ADCG); Abubaker Seddiq Al Khoori, Group CEO of ADCG; and Dr. Mishal Al Qasimi, CEO of the Specialized Rehabilitation Hospital and Health Shield Medical Center.

Expanding rehabilitation and specialty care

The extension will be built next to the existing hospital and will substantially increase SRH’s ability to deliver integrated rehabilitation and specialty services.

The expanded facility will combine inpatient rehabilitation, outpatient specialty clinics, orthopaedic and musculoskeletal care, neurosciences, sports medicine, physical medicine, and cardiac rehabilitation within a single coordinated care model.

Once completed, the hospital will have more than 230 inpatient rehabilitation beds, over 30 outpatient clinics and treatment rooms, and approximately 12 Bayt Al Qudra rehabilitation gyms.

This expansion will give SRH the highest number of inpatient rehabilitation beds, outpatient rehabilitation clinics, and rehabilitation gyms under one roof in the UAE.

The project will also introduce new outpatient services in neurology, sports medicine, physical medicine, and cardiac rehabilitation for both adults and children.

Patients will benefit from integrated diagnostic, treatment, and rehabilitation pathways without needing referrals to multiple facilities.

In addition, the expansion includes advanced operating theatres, including an “Operating Room of the Future,” designed to support complex orthopaedic and musculoskeletal procedures while ensuring a seamless transition from surgery to rehabilitation.

Supporting Abu Dhabi’s healthcare ambitions

Abubaker Seddiq Al Khoori said investments in specialized healthcare are essential for strengthening the resilience and long-term sustainability of health systems.

He noted that the expansion demonstrates ADCG’s confidence in Abu Dhabi’s vision for advanced healthcare and its commitment to building institutions capable of delivering world-class specialized services while reducing the need for patients to seek treatment abroad.

Khalifa Al Mazrouei added that SRH has earned a strong reputation for rehabilitation outcomes and clinical excellence.

He said the new development will enable the hospital to serve more patients from across the UAE and the wider region while supporting Abu Dhabi’s ambitions to become a leading destination for medical tourism through integrated surgical, rehabilitation, and outpatient services.

Dr. Mishal Al Qasimi explained that the hospital’s 2026 organizational theme, “Growth Through Learning,” has guided every aspect of the expansion.

According to him, the project builds on lessons learned from patients, families, and multidisciplinary teams to create more responsive systems and improve care for individuals with increasingly complex rehabilitation needs.

Aligned with wider healthcare development

The expansion supports Abu Dhabi Vision 2030 by improving access to specialized care, enhancing patient outcomes, and strengthening healthcare infrastructure.

It also complements the emirate’s broader investment in advanced healthcare facilities.

Earlier this month, Abu Dhabi also broke ground on the new SEHA Corniche Hospital, part of the emirate’s dedicated medical city for women and children’s healthcare, highlighting continued investment in specialized treatment centers and integrated models of care.

title.rendered: Aster DM Healthcare launches life-stage women’s health programme across UAE

content.rendered:
[et_pb_section fb_built=”1″ _builder_version=”4.27.5″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”][et_pb_row _builder_version=”4.27.5″ _module_preset=”default” custom_margin=”6px|auto||auto||” custom_padding=”15px|||41px||” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”][et_pb_column type=”4_4″ _builder_version=”4.27.4″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”][et_pb_text _builder_version=”4.27.4″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”]

UAE – Aster DM Healthcare has introduced a comprehensive women’s health programme across its UAE network, bringing together preventive care, specialist treatment, and long-term wellness support under a single, coordinated framework.

The initiative combines “Care for Her” by Aster Hospitals & Clinics and “Elle by Medcare,” a premium programme offered through Medcare hospitals and medical centres.

Together, the services are designed to support women from adolescence through menopause and beyond, making them among the region’s most comprehensive life-stage women’s healthcare programmes.

Integrated care across every stage of life

Speaking during the launch, Alisha Moopen, Managing Director and Group CEO of Aster DM Healthcare, said many women struggle to access timely health guidance because they often balance family, work, and other responsibilities while living far from their support systems.

She noted that Aster has drawn on its extensive experience in women’s healthcare to create an integrated network that supports women throughout every stage of life.

Whether helping parents navigate adolescent health, supporting expectant mothers during pregnancy, or caring for women experiencing menopause, the programme connects specialists across multiple disciplines to deliver coordinated care.

Moopen added that women naturally take on leadership roles within their families and communities, making informed healthcare decisions equally important.

“This programme is about giving women the knowledge and confidence to better understand their bodies, anticipate future health needs, make informed decisions, and support the wellbeing of their families,” she said.

Personalised clinical pathways

The programme follows four age-specific care pathways covering teenagers and women in their twenties, young adults, perimenopause, and menopause.

Each stage includes preventive screening, specialist consultations, and tailored treatment plans addressing hormonal, reproductive, metabolic, mental, thyroid, and sexual health.

Care for Her is available at Aster Hospital Al Mankhool, Aster Hospital Al Qusais, and several Aster Clinics across Dubai.

Patients receive coordinated care from consultation and diagnostics through treatment, follow-up, and long-term wellness monitoring with dedicated care coordinators.

Meanwhile, Elle by Medcare offers a more personalised, concierge-style experience through Medcare Royal Specialty Hospital, Medcare Women & Children Hospital, Medcare Hospital Sharjah, Medcare Sheikh Saqr Al Qasimi Hospital, and selected Medcare Medical Centres.

Women begin with a gynaecology consultation before accessing specialists in endocrinology, cardiology, dermatology, internal medicine, mental health, and other fields as needed.

Expanding women’s healthcare services

As part of the initiative, Aster DM Healthcare will also establish dedicated Adolescence and Menopause Clinics to address two often-overlooked stages of women’s health through education, early intervention, and long-term care planning.

The programme will further support communities through school outreach, corporate wellness initiatives, educational workshops, and awareness campaigns that encourage preventive healthcare and improve health literacy.

The launch comes as Aster DM Healthcare continues expanding its healthcare footprint.

The company recently reaffirmed its long-term growth strategy, targeting 15,000 hospital beds by FY2030 following its merger with Quality Care India while continuing to strengthen specialised healthcare services across its Middle East operations.

title.rendered: Thumbay Group expands specialized care hub in Fujairah with historic spine surgery milestone

content.rendered:
[et_pb_section fb_built=”1″ _builder_version=”4.27.5″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”][et_pb_row _builder_version=”4.27.5″ _module_preset=”default” custom_margin=”6px|auto||auto||” custom_padding=”15px|||41px||” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”][et_pb_column type=”4_4″ _builder_version=”4.27.4″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”][et_pb_text _builder_version=”4.27.4″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”]

UAE—Thumbay Hospital Fujairah has successfully performed the first reported Awake Percutaneous Transforaminal Endoscopic Discectomy and Lumbar Interbody Fusion (PETLIF) in the Northern Emirates using an advanced expandable titanium cage.

The image-guided, minimally invasive procedure marks a significant milestone in the region’s spine surgery services and expands access to advanced treatment closer to home.

The surgery was carried out on a 40-year-old patient suffering from severe sciatica caused by an L4-L5 disc herniation.

The patient had endured persistent pain for 14 months and had failed to respond to conservative treatment.

Surgeons completed the entire procedure through a 16 mm incision while the patient remained fully awake, eliminating the need for general anaesthesia.

Within minutes of the operation, the patient reported complete relief from the debilitating leg pain and was able to walk independently in the recovery area.

The small incision and rapid mobilisation highlighted the advantages of modern minimally invasive spine surgery over conventional open procedures.

Real-time patient feedback enhances surgical precision

Unlike traditional spinal fusion surgery, the patient remained conscious throughout the operation and communicated with the surgical team in real time.

This allowed surgeons to continuously monitor neurological function while reducing the physiological stress and potential risks associated with general anaesthesia.

As a result, patients may experience fewer complications, shorter hospital stays, and a quicker return to their daily activities.

The procedure was led by Dr. Hillol Kanti Pal, Consultant Neurosurgeon at Thumbay Hospital Fujairah, with support from anaesthesiologists Dr. Azharuddin and Dr. Ravindra.

“What stood out in this case was not just the technology but the patient himself,” said Dr. Pal.

“He stayed awake throughout the procedure, talking with us as we worked and telling us how his leg felt in real time. That feedback is invaluable during spine surgery. Seeing him walk out of recovery free from pain after more than a year was immensely rewarding.”

Expanding advanced healthcare services

Mr. Akbar Moideen Thumbay, Vice President of the Healthcare Division at Thumbay Group, said the achievement reflects the group’s commitment to making advanced medical care accessible across the Northern Emirates.

“Our goal has always been to bring world-class healthcare closer to the communities we serve so patients no longer need to travel long distances for highly specialised treatment,” he said.

“We will continue investing in advanced technology, skilled professionals, and innovative techniques that improve patient outcomes.”

The procedure comes as Thumbay Hospital Fujairah continues to strengthen its specialist services.

Just days ago, the hospital celebrated its 19th anniversary by launching a Respiratory Medicine Department, opening a Well Woman Clinic, and introducing the Thumbay Kids Privilege Card to expand preventive and family healthcare services.

The hospital also recently joined a group of private healthcare providers that signed memoranda of understanding with the UAE Ministry of Health and Prevention to strengthen collaboration on emergency preparedness and ensure continuity of healthcare services during national crises.

Patients experiencing chronic back pain, sciatica, or disc-related disorders are encouraged to seek specialist assessment to determine whether minimally invasive spine surgery is an appropriate treatment option.

title.rendered: Mayo Clinic’s NEJM study advances precision oncology for relapsed myeloma

content.rendered:
[et_pb_section fb_built=”1″ _builder_version=”4.27.5″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”][et_pb_row _builder_version=”4.27.5″ _module_preset=”default” custom_margin=”6px|auto||auto||” custom_padding=”15px|||41px||” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”][et_pb_column type=”4_4″ _builder_version=”4.27.4″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”][et_pb_text _builder_version=”4.27.4″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”]

UAE—A new study led by Mayo Clinic and published in the New England Journal of Medicine has reported promising results for patients with extramedullary multiple myeloma, one of the most aggressive and difficult-to-treat forms of blood cancer.

Conducted in the UAE, amid growing discussions on oncology innovation, the findings highlight how a dual-antibody approach can trigger strong and lasting immune responses in patients with previously limited treatment options.

Targeting cancer through a dual immune Pathway

Researchers tested a combination of two engineered antibodies, talquetamab and teclistamab, designed to activate T cells in two complementary ways.

These antibodies guide immune cells directly toward myeloma cells and encourage them to attack through distinct biological pathways.

Unlike CAR-T therapy, which requires patient-specific cell modification and lengthy manufacturing, this treatment is delivered as a ready-to-use infusion, making it more accessible in standard hospital settings.

According to study author Dr. Shaji Kumar of Mayo Clinic Comprehensive Cancer Center, the approach reflects a shift in how immune therapies are designed.

He noted that engaging T cells through dual mechanisms creates a stronger and more coordinated attack against cancer cells, especially in cases that have resisted multiple prior treatments.

Clinical trial results show high response rates

The trial enrolled 90 patients with confirmed extramedullary multiple myeloma, verified using PET and MRI imaging.

Among them, 79% showed a measurable response to treatment, while 54% achieved no detectable disease in imaging or blood tests.

In addition, nearly two-thirds of responders-maintained disease control after one year, a significant outcome for a condition that typically progresses within months.

Researchers emphasized that the study was the first large prospective trial focused exclusively on true extramedullary disease, rather than mixed forms of myeloma, allowing for more precise evaluation of outcomes.

Safety profile and ongoing questions

While the results were encouraging, the study also reported notable safety concerns.

Infections emerged as one of the most significant adverse effects, underscoring the need for careful monitoring and supportive care during treatment.

Researchers stressed that managing immune suppression will be essential as the therapy moves forward.

Looking ahead, scientists are now exploring whether this dual-target strategy could be introduced earlier in the disease course and whether safety can be improved through better infection prevention protocols.

They are also investigating whether similar “two-lock, one-key” immune designs could be adapted for other hard-to-treat cancers, potentially expanding the reach of this approach across oncology.

title.rendered: Jentayu Sustainables exits healthcare with US$414,000 sale of Ohana Hospital unit

content.rendered:
[et_pb_section fb_built=”1″ _builder_version=”4.27.5″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”][et_pb_row _builder_version=”4.27.5″ _module_preset=”default” custom_margin=”6px|auto||auto||” custom_padding=”15px|||41px||” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”][et_pb_column type=”4_4″ _builder_version=”4.27.4″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”][et_pb_text _builder_version=”4.27.4″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”]

MALAYSIA—Jentayu Sustainables Bhd has announced its complete exit from the healthcare sector after agreeing to sell its entire stake in Ultimate Forte Sdn Bhd (UFSB), the operator of Ohana Specialist Hospital in Kuala Lumpur, to Lourdes Medical Centre for RM1.75 million (US$414,000).

The move marks a significant strategic shift as the company sharpens its focus on expanding its renewable energy portfolio.

Ohana Specialist Hospital is a 30-bed private facility that specializes in paediatrics as well as obstetrics and gynaecology.

Jentayu said the disposal forms part of its long-term plan to streamline operations and concentrate resources on its core clean energy business.

The company first ventured into healthcare in 2021 when it was still known as Ipmuda Bhd.

At the time, it proposed a rights issue to finance investments in both renewable energy and healthcare.

It later completed the acquisition of UFSB in February 2022 for RM18 million (US$4.26 million) as part of its diversification strategy.

Financial performance influenced decision

The healthcare business has struggled financially in recent years.

For the financial year ended June 30, 2025, UFSB recorded a net loss of RM2.05 million (US$485,000) and reported net liabilities of RM7.22 million (US$1.71 million).

As part of the transaction, Jentayu will also assume RM1.18 million (US$279,000) in liabilities owed to UFSB’s creditors up to April 20, 2026.

Despite taking on these obligations, the company expects to recognize a gain of approximately RM2.37 million (US$561,000) from the disposal after accounting for the subsidiary’s net liabilities.

Lourdes Medical Centre, which is wholly owned by Rayyan Medical Services Sdn Bhd, officially assumed responsibility for the hospital’s management and operations on April 20, 2026.

Its sole director, Datuk Muhammad Rayyan Abdullah, also serves as a director of UFSB.

However, Jentayu clarified that the disposal does not constitute a related-party transaction and does not require shareholder approval.

Hospital faced operational setbacks

Jentayu’s healthcare venture encountered several operational challenges during its ownership of the hospital.

Slightly more than a year after acquiring the facility, the Ministry of Health revoked Ohana Specialist Hospital’s operating licence because of non-compliance with regulatory requirements.

The hospital remained closed for more than two months before the licence was later reinstated after management introduced stronger governance measures and operational improvements.

Although healthcare generated about 57% of the group’s revenue during the first quarter ended March 31, 2025, the segment also contributed nearly 29% of the company’s quarterly net loss of RM4.19 million (US$992,000).

Those results highlighted the financial strain the business placed on the broader group.

Renewable energy becomes top priority

The divestment aligns with Jentayu’s broader restructuring efforts as it channels more capital into renewable energy projects, particularly its hydropower developments in Sabah.

The company has continued to raise funds and reorganize its business to support these long-term investments while reducing exposure to non-core operations.

Recent corporate announcements also include financing initiatives for its Oriole Hydro project, underscoring management’s commitment to expanding its clean energy portfolio.

Market analysts have identified the disposal as one of the key corporate developments influencing investor attention this week, describing it as part of Jentayu’s ongoing transformation into a renewable energy-focused company.

Jentayu’s shares closed unchanged at 25.5 sen on Friday, giving the company a market capitalization of approximately RM138.8 million (US$32.9 million).

The stock has declined 13.56% since the beginning of the year.

title.rendered: Why the Gulf needs more hospice and palliative care as its population ages

content.rendered:
[et_pb_section fb_built=”1″ _builder_version=”4.27.5″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}”][et_pb_row _builder_version=”4.27.5″ _module_preset=”default” custom_margin=”6px|auto||auto||” custom_padding=”2px|||41px||” global_colors_info=”{}”][et_pb_column type=”4_4″ _builder_version=”4.27.4″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}”][et_pb_text _builder_version=”4.27.4″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}”]

By Mark Adams, CEO of Clemenceau Medical Center 

UAE—Around the world, conversations about serious illness often revolve around treatment, with doctors discussing available therapies, exploring new options, and planning the next course of action.

However, when medical treatment can no longer change the outcome, attention rarely shifts to equally important questions such as where patients want to spend their final days, who they want beside them, and how they wish to live the remainder of their lives.

Across the Gulf, those questions remain difficult to answer.

Although countries in the region have invested heavily in world-class hospitals, advanced medical technology, and specialised treatment, support for people nearing the end of life has not developed at the same pace.

As a result, many patients and their families still lack the care they need beyond hospital walls.

A Gap Between Patient Wishes and Reality

When asked where they would prefer to spend their final days, most people choose home rather than a hospital.

They want to remain in familiar surroundings with their loved ones close by.

This preference is universal, but it carries even greater significance in Gulf societies, where family plays a central role in culture, faith, and caregiving.

Despite these preferences, many people across the UAE and the wider Gulf still die in hospitals.

This is often not because they choose to, but because community-based hospice and palliative care services remain extremely limited.

Research consistently shows that patients in the UAE who wish to receive end-of-life care at home rarely have that opportunity.

The country has very few community palliative care teams or dedicated hospice facilities outside major hospitals, leaving families with limited alternatives.

Closing this gap would not only improve the quality of life for patients but also provide much-needed support for families while easing pressure on healthcare systems.

Progress has begun, but access remains limited

The UAE has taken important steps to strengthen palliative care over the past two decades.

In 2007, Tawam Hospital in Abu Dhabi established the country’s first comprehensive palliative care programme, laying the foundation for further development.

Since then, services have expanded gradually. However, they remain concentrated within oncology departments in a small number of hospitals, mainly in Abu Dhabi and Dubai.

Consequently, many patients living with advanced heart disease, dementia, chronic respiratory illness, and other life-limiting conditions still have limited access to specialised palliative care.

The World Health Organization also classifies the UAE as having only isolated palliative care services relative to the country’s overall healthcare needs.

Nevertheless, encouraging progress continues.

In late 2023, Burjeel Holdings signed a landmark partnership with London’s St. Christopher’s Hospice, widely recognised as the birthplace of modern hospice care, to establish the UAE’s first dedicated hospice facility in Abu Dhabi.

The project aims to create a compassionate centre for end-of-life care while supporting patients, families, and healthcare professionals.

Although this marks a significant milestone, a single hospice cannot meet the needs of a region with tens of millions of residents.

An aging population will increase demand

The need for palliative and hospice care is expected to grow rapidly over the coming decades.

Although the Gulf currently has a relatively young population, demographic trends point to a significant shift.

According to PwC’s Middle East Megatrends analysis, one in every five GCC nationals will be elderly by 2050, representing a tenfold increase from current levels.

As populations age, chronic illnesses such as cancer, cardiovascular disease, diabetes, and dementia become more common.

Many of these conditions eventually require palliative care rather than curative treatment.

Healthcare systems across the Gulf have invested extensively in diagnosing and treating these diseases.

However, they have devoted far fewer resources to supporting patients whose illnesses can no longer be cured and to helping families manage the physical and emotional challenges that follow.

Building this infrastructure now will help healthcare systems prepare for rising demand rather than struggle to catch up later.

Lessons from the UK’s Hospice Model

The United Kingdom offers one of the world’s most established examples of hospice and palliative care.

The movement began in 1967 when Dame Cicely Saunders founded St. Christopher’s Hospice in London.

Since then, the country has developed a network of more than 200 hospices alongside community-based services such as Macmillan Cancer Support.

Through this model, specialist nurses work closely with general practitioners and families, helping patients manage symptoms, receive emotional support, and remain at home whenever possible.

The results have been impressive.

Studies show that specialist community palliative care increases the likelihood of patients dying in their preferred place by around 50%.

At the same time, healthcare costs during the final year of life fall by approximately 20%.

These outcomes demonstrate that better patient experiences and lower healthcare costs can go hand in hand.

Even so, the UK model cannot simply be replicated in the Gulf. The region’s cultural and religious traditions shape how families approach illness, caregiving, and death, requiring solutions that reflect local values.

Building a Hospice Model that reflects Gulf culture

Islamic teachings view death as a natural transition and emphasize compassion, dignity, and family involvement throughout the final stages of life.

In many Emirati and Arab households, caring for a dying relative is regarded as both a family responsibility and a spiritual duty.

These traditions naturally support many of the principles of palliative care.

Families already value caring for loved ones at home, surrounded by relatives and supported by faith.

What they often lack is the clinical expertise and practical assistance needed to make home-based care possible.

A successful Gulf hospice model should therefore focus on strengthening community services that work alongside families rather than replacing them.

This approach would include specially trained community nurses; palliative care physicians who understand both clinical practice and Islamic ethics; grief counsellors familiar with local bereavement traditions; and accessible Arabic-language resources.

It should also ensure that care remains culturally sensitive and respects gender preferences whenever appropriate.

Developing these services is well within reach if governments and healthcare providers commit the necessary investment and long-term planning.

 Encouraging open conversations about end-of-life care

Alongside expanding services, the Gulf also needs to encourage more open conversations about end-of-life care.

In many healthcare settings across the region, families and clinicians often try to protect patients from learning the full extent of a serious diagnosis.

Although this approach stems from compassion and a desire to preserve hope, it can also prevent patients from expressing their wishes, making important personal decisions, or spending their remaining time in the environment they would have chosen.

High-quality palliative care creates opportunities for these conversations while respecting cultural values and individual beliefs.

Rather than signaling the end of treatment, it focuses on improving comfort, preserving dignity, managing symptoms, and ensuring that patients continue to receive compassionate care throughout the final stage of life.

Creating space for these discussions allows patients, families, and healthcare professionals to make informed decisions together while ensuring that end-of-life care reflects each person’s values, preferences, and dignity.

title.rendered: MTRH expands specialized diagnostics with new ISO 15189 quality standards from KENAS

content.rendered:
[et_pb_section fb_built=”1″ _builder_version=”4.27.5″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”][et_pb_row _builder_version=”4.27.5″ _module_preset=”default” custom_margin=”6px|auto||auto||” custom_padding=”15px|||41px||” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”][et_pb_column type=”4_4″ _builder_version=”4.27.4″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”][et_pb_text _builder_version=”4.27.4″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”]

KENYA—Moi Teaching and Referral Hospital (MTRH) has achieved a major milestone after its Directorate of Laboratory and Pathology Services secured its third-cycle re-accreditation to the ISO 15189:2022 standard from the Kenya Accreditation Service (KENAS).

The achievement follows a rigorous four-day external assessment conducted between June 23 and June 26, 2026, during which KENAS auditors evaluated the laboratory’s quality management systems, technical competence, and compliance with international standards.

The assessment team recommended accreditation for 100% of the scope submitted, covering hematology, clinical chemistry, immunology, parasitology, bacteriology, mycobacteriology, blood transfusion, and histopathology.

Maintaining international standards

The latest accreditation marks another milestone for MTRH, which first earned KENAS accreditation in 2018 and has consistently maintained internationally accepted standards for laboratory testing and pathology services.

The recognition demonstrates the hospital’s continued focus on producing accurate, reliable, and timely diagnostic results while strengthening patient safety and quality assurance.

Laboratory accreditation under ISO 15189:2022 requires medical laboratories to demonstrate technical competence, effective quality management systems, and continuous improvement.

Compliance with the standard also enhances confidence among clinicians and patients by ensuring laboratory results meet internationally accepted benchmarks.

Florence Tum, Director of Laboratory and Pathology Services at MTRH, credited the accomplishment to the dedication, professionalism, and teamwork demonstrated by laboratory staff throughout the assessment process.

She noted that maintaining accreditation requires continuous monitoring, staff training, adherence to quality procedures, and a culture of ongoing improvement.

MTRH Chief Executive Officer Dr. Philip Kirwa also congratulated the laboratory team, saying the successful re-accreditation reflects the hospital’s unwavering commitment to quality healthcare, patient safety, and service excellence.

He added that maintaining internationally recognized laboratory standards strengthens MTRH’s position as one of Kenya’s leading referral hospitals and a regional centre for specialized healthcare.

Meanwhile, KENAS assessment team leader Julie Ochola commended the Directorate for sustaining a strong quality culture and consistently meeting the stringent requirements for retaining accreditation.

Hospital Expands Specialized Healthcare

The laboratory milestone comes as MTRH continues to strengthen its position as a national referral and teaching hospital through investments in specialized healthcare services and infrastructure.

Earlier this month, the hospital successfully performed Kenya’s first Transjugular Intrahepatic Portosystemic Shunt (TIPS) procedure, a minimally invasive intervention used to treat severe complications associated with advanced liver disease.

The landmark procedure was made possible through investments in advanced medical technology, specialist training, and collaboration under the AMPATH Radiology Partnership, further expanding access to highly specialized care within Kenya.

In addition, government officials recently confirmed that construction of the new 2,000-bed MTRH Multi-Speciality Hospital remains on schedule for completion in early 2027.

Once operational, the facility is expected to become Kenya’s largest hospital, significantly increasing the country’s capacity for specialized treatment, medical training, and research while strengthening MTRH’s role as a regional healthcare hub.

title.rendered: Burjeel Holdings issues US$500M debut sukuk to fund healthcare expansion

content.rendered:
[et_pb_section fb_built=”1″ _builder_version=”4.27.5″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}”][et_pb_row _builder_version=”4.27.5″ _module_preset=”default” custom_margin=”6px|auto||auto||” custom_padding=”15px|||41px||” global_colors_info=”{}”][et_pb_column type=”4_4″ _builder_version=”4.27.4″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}”][et_pb_text _builder_version=”4.27.4″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}”]

UAE—Burjeel Holdings, one of the GCC’s leading super-specialty healthcare providers listed on the Abu Dhabi Securities Exchange, has successfully priced its inaugural US$500 million senior unsecured Sukuk under Regulation S.

The five-year Islamic bond, which matures in 2031, marks the first issuance under the group’s newly established US$1.5 billion Senior Unsecured Sukuk Programme.

Strong investor appetite boosts pricing

The transaction drew robust interest from both regional and international investors, with the orderbook reaching approximately US$1.6 billion, making the offering about 3.2 times oversubscribed.

Strong demand enabled Burjeel to tighten pricing from the initial guidance in the mid-7% range before setting the Sukuk at a 7.000% profit rate and a 7.125% yield.

According to the company, the transaction achieved the lowest five-year yield secured by a GCC-based private non-investment-grade corporate issuer since 2020.

The issuance also represents the first Sukuk by a healthcare provider in the Middle East and North Africa since 2018, reflecting renewed investor confidence in the regional healthcare sector and debt capital markets.

International investors received 61% of the final allocation, led by buyers from the United Kingdom (34%) and US offshore investors (24%), while GCC-based investors accounted for the remaining 39%.

The broad geographic participation highlights growing confidence in Burjeel’s business model and the UAE’s capital markets.

Funding growth and refinancing

Burjeel plans to use the net proceeds in line with the offering documents, including refinancing existing debt while supporting the group’s long-term strategic priorities.

The funding is expected to strengthen the company’s financial flexibility and capital structure as it continues to invest in advanced clinical services, research, medical education, and artificial intelligence-enabled healthcare solutions.

The Sukuk carries corporate ratings of BB+ from S&P Global Ratings and Ba2 from Moody’s Ratings.

These first-time ratings were assigned only days before the issuance, alongside the launch of the US$1.5 billion Sukuk programme, providing the company with a flexible Shariah-compliant platform to access international debt markets.

Commenting on the transaction, Chairman and CEO Dr. Shamsheer Vayalil said the strong investor response reflects confidence in Burjeel’s strategy, financial fundamentals and long-term growth prospects.

He added that the successful issuance expands the company’s access to global capital markets while providing additional flexibility to invest in advanced healthcare services, research, medical education and AI-driven innovation.

Recent developments support expansion

The Sukuk comes shortly after Burjeel established its inaugural US$1.5 billion programme through Burjeel Sukuk Limited, a special purpose vehicle created to facilitate future issuances.

The programme has been admitted to trading on the London Stock Exchange’s International Securities Market, strengthening the company’s ability to diversify its funding sources and support future expansion.

The financing also follows a solid start to 2026 for the healthcare group.

In its first-quarter financial results, Burjeel reported revenue of AED 1.3 billion (US$354 million), EBITDA of AED 201 million (US$55 million), and net profit of AED 57 million (US$15.5 million), supported by higher patient volumes, improved operating efficiency, and continued investment in specialized healthcare services.

Citi, Emirates NBD Capital and First Abu Dhabi Bank served as Joint Global Coordinators for the transaction.

Emirates NBD Capital and First Abu Dhabi Bank also acted as Sukuk Structuring Agents, while Abu Dhabi Commercial Bank, Abu Dhabi Islamic Bank, Dubai Islamic Bank, RAKBANK and Sharjah Islamic Bank served as Joint Lead Managers and Bookrunners.

title.rendered: JHAH introduces advanced fusion-guided prostate biopsy technology to improve early cancer detection in Saudi Arabia

content.rendered:
[et_pb_section fb_built=”1″ _builder_version=”4.27.5″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”][et_pb_row _builder_version=”4.27.5″ _module_preset=”default” custom_margin=”6px|auto||auto||” custom_padding=”15px|||41px||” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”][et_pb_column type=”4_4″ _builder_version=”4.27.4″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”][et_pb_text _builder_version=”4.27.4″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”]

SAUDI ARABIA—Johns Hopkins Aramco Healthcare (JHAH) has become the first hospital in Saudi Arabia’s Eastern Province to offer MRI-ultrasound fusion-guided prostate biopsy using the transperineal approach, a combination available at only a limited number of hospitals worldwide.

The new service is expected to strengthen prostate cancer diagnosis in a region that continues to record the highest incidence of the disease in the Kingdom.

According to data from the Saudi Cancer Registry, the Eastern Province has consistently reported the highest rates of prostate cancer nationwide.

The Saudi Health Council’s 2023 Cancer Incidence Report also identified prostate cancer as the second most commonly diagnosed cancer among Saudi men, accounting for 7.6% of all cancers diagnosed in this population.

Despite this, many cases are still detected at advanced stages, making treatment more challenging and reducing the likelihood of favourable outcomes.

To help address this challenge, JHAH has introduced a technology that combines detailed prostate MRI scans with real-time ultrasound imaging.

This allows physicians to identify suspicious lesions with greater precision and target them directly during biopsy procedures rather than relying on random tissue sampling.

Improving accuracy while reducing risks

The new diagnostic approach aligns with recommendations from the European Association of Urology and the American Urological Association.

Research supporting these guidelines has shown that targeted biopsies can detect nearly 30% more clinically significant prostate cancers while reducing the diagnosis of low-risk cancers that may lead to unnecessary treatment by approximately 17%.

In addition, JHAH is using the transperineal biopsy technique, in which the biopsy needle passes through the skin between the scrotum and anus rather than through the rectum.

This method significantly lowers the risk of infection and sepsis commonly associated with traditional transrectal biopsies.

It also reduces the need for preventive antibiotic use and provides better access to areas of the prostate that conventional methods can sometimes miss.

Because the procedure requires fewer tissue samples, patients often experience less discomfort and face a lower risk of complications.

Hospital leaders believe these advantages could encourage more men to seek screening and evaluation earlier, particularly in a region where late-stage diagnosis remains common.

Dr. Tareq Al-Tartir, Consultant Urologist at JHAH, said the technology enables physicians to provide highly reliable diagnoses while minimizing patient discomfort and procedural risks.

“Detecting significant prostate cancer accurately and at an earlier stage can dramatically improve treatment options and outcomes,” he said. “This is precision medicine delivering meaningful benefits for patients.”

Expanding precision oncology services

The new biopsy capability is one of the first services introduced through JHAH’s Oncology Center of Excellence, which was established in partnership with Johns Hopkins Medicine’s Sidney Kimmel Comprehensive Cancer Center.

The center focuses on breast, colorectal, and prostate cancers while bringing internationally recognized diagnostic and treatment standards to Saudi Arabia.

The prostate cancer program also offers advanced multiparametric MRI imaging, fusion-guided biopsies, robotic-assisted surgery, and access to precision medicine approaches.

The launch follows a series of recent investments by JHAH aimed at strengthening specialized healthcare services.

In April, the organization opened a new PET/CT facility to enhance cancer diagnosis, treatment planning, and disease monitoring through advanced imaging technologies.

Hospital leaders said the addition supports faster and more accurate clinical decision-making across oncology and other specialties.

Dr. Howard Podolsky, Chief Executive Officer of JHAH, said the introduction of MRI-ultrasound fusion biopsy reflects the organization’s commitment to advancing precision medicine and delivering patient-centered care.

“By investing in advanced technology and world-class procedures, we are improving diagnostic accuracy and helping redefine the standard of prostate cancer care in the region,” he said.

The initiative also supports Saudi Arabia’s Vision 2030 Health Sector Transformation Program by expanding access to advanced cancer services within the Kingdom and reducing the need for patients to seek specialized care abroad.

JHAH encourages men aged 50 years and older, as well as those aged 45 and above with a family history of prostate cancer, to discuss screening and prostate health with their healthcare providers.

title.rendered: JOOTRH deploys automated blood analyzer to cut transfusion screening to 35 minutes

content.rendered:
[et_pb_section fb_built=”1″ _builder_version=”4.27.5″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”][et_pb_row _builder_version=”4.27.5″ _module_preset=”default” custom_margin=”6px|auto||auto||” custom_padding=”15px|||41px||” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”][et_pb_column type=”4_4″ _builder_version=”4.27.4″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”][et_pb_text _builder_version=”4.27.4″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”]

KENYA—Jaramogi Oginga Odinga Teaching and Referral Hospital (JOOTRH) is enhancing blood safety and transfusion services in Kisumu County to better support patients with sickle cell disease (SCD), a significant burden for families in the Lake Region.

A major step in this effort came in March 2026 with the installation of an automated blood screening analyzer that has significantly reduced the time required to screen donated blood.

The new technology can complete blood screening within 20 to 35 minutes using advanced antigen-antibody detection methods, enabling clinicians to access safe blood more quickly for emergency and routine transfusions.

According to Kenneth Youth Onyango, a blood screening expert at JOOTRH, every donated unit undergoes comprehensive testing before it is cleared for use.

“Screening is done to detect infections such as HIV, Hepatitis B, Hepatitis C, and syphilis. Any infected blood is discarded because patient safety comes first,” he said.

Faster screening enhances patient safety

In addition to screening for infectious diseases, the hospital performs blood grouping and compatibility testing to ensure patients receive the correct blood type.

Donated blood is stored at temperatures ranging between 3°C and 6°C before it is processed into different blood components.

Red blood cells are then used for transfusions and exchange procedures, both of which play a critical role in the management of sickle cell disease.

The investment comes at a time when demand for specialized sickle cell services is growing in western Kenya.

Patients living with the condition often require repeated transfusions to manage severe anaemia, prevent complications, and improve quality of life.

At the Victoria Hospital Annex, JOOTRH’s dedicated centre for sickle cell disease and other blood disorders, safe blood supplies are supported by the Spectra Optia Apheresis System to enable advanced treatment.

Since the technology was introduced, 35 patients have successfully undergone red blood cell exchange procedures.

The hospital became the first public health facility in Kenya to deploy the system, significantly expanding access to specialized care in the region.

Advanced treatment reduces complications

Dr. Brenda Misore, a paediatric oncologist at JOOTRH, explained that apheresis works by removing sickled red blood cells and replacing them with healthy donor cells.

The procedure lowers the proportion of sickled cells from as high as 80 per cent to below 30 per cent, reducing the risk of complications such as stroke, acute chest syndrome, severe anaemia, and recurrent pain crises.

However, each procedure may require between six and ten units of blood, underscoring the importance of sustained voluntary blood donation.

Recent government assessments have highlighted JOOTRH’s growing role in specialized sickle cell care.

Earlier this month, Principal Secretary for Medical Services Dr. Ouma Oluga led county health officials on a tour of the facility, where they reviewed ongoing investments in advanced treatment services.

The government has also announced plans to transform JOOTRH into a centre of excellence for sickle cell disease care in Africa as part of broader efforts to strengthen specialized healthcare under Universal Health Coverage reforms.

Addressing a high disease burden

The need for these services remains urgent. Estimates show that approximately one in every fourteen children born in Kisumu has sickle cell disease, while nearly 20 percent of the population carries the sickle cell trait.

Nationally, health officials estimate that about 14,000 children are born with the condition every year, particularly in high-burden counties across western, Nyanza, and coastal regions.

As the hospital continues to expand specialized treatment capacity, reliable access to screened blood remains central to patient care.

Safe blood supplies support routine transfusions, emergency interventions, and advanced procedures such as apheresis, enabling more patients living with sickle cell disease to access timely treatment closer to home.

title.rendered: Medcare becomes first UAE healthcare provider to deploy InterSystems IntelliCare EHR

content.rendered:
[et_pb_section fb_built=”1″ _builder_version=”4.27.5″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”][et_pb_row _builder_version=”4.27.5″ _module_preset=”default” custom_margin=”6px|auto||auto||” custom_padding=”15px|||41px||” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”][et_pb_column type=”4_4″ _builder_version=”4.27.4″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”][et_pb_text _builder_version=”4.27.4″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”]

UAE—Medcare Hospitals and Medical Centres, the premium healthcare arm of Aster DM Healthcare, has signed a strategic partnership with InterSystems to deploy InterSystems IntelliCare™, becoming the first healthcare provider in the UAE and the wider region to implement a next-generation, AI-first electronic health record (EHR) platform.

The memorandum of understanding was signed by Alisha Moopen, Managing Director and Group CEO of Aster DM Healthcare, and Ali Abi Raad, Managing Director of InterSystems Middle East, India and South Africa, in the presence of senior officials from both organisations.

AI embedded at the core of clinical care

While many healthcare providers have introduced artificial intelligence through standalone applications, diagnostic tools, and workflow automation solutions, Medcare’s adoption of IntelliCare marks a significant shift towards a fully integrated AI-powered healthcare ecosystem.

Unlike conventional EHR systems that add AI as an extra feature, IntelliCare places artificial intelligence at the centre of the clinical workflow.

The platform is designed to streamline operations, improve interoperability across hospitals, clinics, laboratories, and insurers, and reduce the administrative burden on healthcare professionals.

The move forms part of Medcare’s broader digital transformation strategy and reinforces its commitment to improving clinical outcomes, operational efficiency, and patient-centred care.

Alisha Moopen said the organisation has consistently invested in advanced technologies that enable physicians and caregivers to prioritise patients and deliver better outcomes.

She noted that adopting an AI-first EHR platform represents a major step towards transforming healthcare delivery.

According to Moopen, intelligent systems will increasingly support healthcare professionals by reducing paperwork, generating meaningful insights, and allowing more time for patient care.

Supporting physicians through intelligent automation

The IntelliCare platform will help clinicians access patient information more efficiently while automating clinical documentation.

Using AI-powered information retrieval, natural language interaction, and ambient documentation capabilities, physicians will be able to review diagnoses, medications, test results, procedures, and clinical notes more quickly.

Future versions of the platform will incorporate agentic AI technologies capable of supporting clinical decision-making and workflow management.

These AI assistants will operate alongside healthcare professionals while maintaining human oversight.

Ali Abi Raad said the latest agreement builds on a partnership that began in 2020 when Medcare adopted the InterSystems TrakCare platform as part of its digital transformation programme.

He described the transition to IntelliCare as the next stage in Medcare’s innovation journey and a sign of the growing relationship between InterSystems and Aster DM Healthcare.

Enhanced Experience for Patients

For patients, the platform is expected to create a more seamless healthcare experience. By reducing time spent on documentation, physicians can devote greater attention to consultations and personalised care.

Access to a unified patient record will also support more informed treatment decisions, better continuity of care, and fewer duplicated tests.

Dr. Shanila Laiju, Group CEO of Medcare Hospitals and Medical Centres, said artificial intelligence is reshaping healthcare globally and that Medcare is committed to ensuring both patients and clinicians benefit from these advances.

She explained that embedding intelligence directly into the clinical ecosystem will help physicians access insights faster, streamline workflows, and spend more time interacting with patients.

The announcement comes as Aster DM Healthcare accelerates its digital transformation and expansion plans across the UAE.

Earlier this year, the group unveiled projects worth AED 1 billion (US$272 million), including two new hospitals in Dubai, an advanced robotic rehabilitation centre, Sharjah’s first private multi-organ transplant centre, and expanded AI-enabled healthcare initiatives.

Since its launch in 2025, IntelliCare has gained international traction, with deployments across eight hospitals operated by Indonesia’s EMC Healthcare.

The platform is also the first unified AI-powered EHR system to receive EU Class IIa Medical Device Regulation certification for clinical safety.

title.rendered: SEHA’s Tawam Hospital hosts region’s first certified low-dose radiotherapy workshop

content.rendered:
[et_pb_section fb_built=”1″ _builder_version=”4.27.5″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”][et_pb_row _builder_version=”4.27.5″ _module_preset=”default” custom_margin=”6px|auto||auto||” custom_padding=”15px|||41px||” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”][et_pb_column type=”4_4″ _builder_version=”4.27.4″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”][et_pb_text _builder_version=”4.27.4″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”]

UAE—SEHA, a subsidiary of PureHealth and one of the Middle East’s largest healthcare providers, has announced that Tawam Hospital will host the UAE’s and the wider region’s first certified workshop on Low-Dose Radiotherapy (LDRT) for benign diseases.

The initiative marks a significant step toward expanding the use of radiation therapy beyond cancer treatment to selected inflammatory and noncancerous conditions.

The three-day programme, developed in collaboration with JointGlow, will bring together radiation oncologists, medical physicists, radiation therapists, informatics specialists, healthcare administrators, and other clinical leaders.

Participants will focus on developing safe and standardized pathways for the use of LDRT in carefully selected benign conditions while aligning practices with international clinical guidelines.

Advancing new uses for radiotherapy

Although research into low-dose radiotherapy for benign diseases has shown promising results, much of the evidence is still being generated through clinical trials.

As a result, healthcare institutions across the region have been cautious in adopting the approach on a wider scale.

SEHA said the workshop will address this gap by establishing what it describes as the region’s first institution-level certification framework for the responsible implementation of LDRT.

The initiative is designed to support evidence-based clinical innovation while ensuring robust governance, patient safety, and quality assurance.

Under the programme, Tawam Hospital will receive institutional certification, while participating clinicians will earn individual certifications.

The workshop will also introduce proposed unified clinical protocols and operational workflows supported by a governance and registry framework.

This system will enable healthcare providers to track patient outcomes, monitor quality indicators, and evaluate long-term clinical effectiveness.

Focus on governance and patient safety

Dr. Khalid Balaraj, Chair of the Oncology Centre at Tawam Hospital, said the initiative reflects SEHA’s commitment to advancing patient-centred and evidence-based care.

“At Tawam Hospital, we remain focused on expanding access to innovative treatments that improve patient outcomes,” he said.

The JointGlow Low-Dose Radiotherapy initiative represents an important step toward offering safe, non-invasive treatment options for selected benign conditions within a structured clinical framework. ”

Dr. Abdulrahman Bin Sumaida, Division Chief of Radiation Oncology at Tawam Hospital, noted that the programme demonstrates the hospital’s readiness to adopt emerging radiotherapy applications in a systematic and outcomes-driven manner.

“Our focus extends beyond implementation. We want to ensure these programmes are scalable, sustainable, and capable of delivering long-term value for both patients and healthcare systems,” he said.

Dr. Khalifa Alkaabi, Consultant in Radiation Oncology at Tawam Hospital, emphasized the importance of strong oversight when introducing new therapeutic approaches.

“Low-Dose Radiotherapy for benign diseases requires rigorous governance and clinical accountability. Through this collaboration, we are ensuring that innovation is introduced safely, consistently, and with measurable impact,” he said.

Building regional expertise

The workshop will feature contributions from leading oncology and radiation oncology specialists from across the UAE, as well as international experts from JointGlow.

Organizers expect the programme to serve as a practical model for future LDRT initiatives across the UAE and the wider Gulf region, with Tawam Hospital playing a key role in training, certification, and quality oversight.

The latest initiative adds to a series of recent innovations at Tawam Hospital aimed at strengthening advanced clinical care.

Earlier this year, the hospital became the first healthcare provider in the UAE to introduce histotripsy, a non-invasive technology that uses focused ultrasound energy to treat liver tumours without surgery, radiotherapy, or chemotherapy.

The technology has already been used to treat patients from the UAE and abroad, reinforcing Tawam Hospital’s position as a regional centre for advanced oncology services.

The launch of the LDRT certification programme further reflects SEHA’s broader strategy of expanding specialized treatment options while supporting clinical research, innovation, and workforce development across the UAE healthcare sector.
