title.rendered: Sidra Medicine debuts Medical Observership Program for healthcare workforce development

content.rendered:
[et_pb_section fb_built=”1″ _builder_version=”4.27.5″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”][et_pb_row _builder_version=”4.27.5″ _module_preset=”default” custom_margin=”6px|auto||auto||” custom_padding=”15px|||41px||” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”][et_pb_column type=”4_4″ _builder_version=”4.27.4″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”][et_pb_text _builder_version=”4.27.4″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”]

QATAR — Sidra Medicine, a member of the Qatar Foundation, is strengthening its commitment to healthcare workforce development through the launch of a new Medical Observership Program and the continued expansion of its Future Doctor Program.

 The two initiatives are designed to create educational pathways for aspiring healthcare professionals, medical students, and experienced practitioners seeking to broaden their knowledge and skills.

Prof. Ibrahim Janahi, Chief Medical Officer and Chair of Medical Education at Sidra Medicine, said education remains a core pillar of the institution’s mission and an essential investment in the future of healthcare.

He noted that providing meaningful learning opportunities allows students, trainees, and healthcare professionals to gain practical insights from experienced clinicians and multidisciplinary teams.

According to him, these experiences help participants develop the skills, confidence, and knowledge required to address the evolving healthcare needs of communities across the region.

New Medical Observership Program opens doors for healthcare professionals

The newly launched Medical Observership Program offers structured observational learning opportunities within one of the region’s leading tertiary academic medical centers.

The initiative is open to physicians, specialists, residents, fellows, medical students, nurses, allied health professionals, academic visitors, and selected high school students.

International applicants may also be considered, subject to institutional requirements and approvals.

Dr. Murtada Hammad, Director of Medical Education Operations at Sidra Medicine, said the program gives participants valuable exposure to specialized healthcare delivery in a world-class academic environment.

Through supervised observation, participants can learn how multidisciplinary teams collaborate, gain insight into patient safety practices, and understand modern clinical and operational workflows.

The observerships are strictly educational and do not involve direct patient care or participation in clinical procedures.

Available placements may include Pediatrics, Pediatric Subspecialties, Women’s Services, Obstetrics and Gynecology, Neonatology, Surgery, and various diagnostic and support departments, depending on availability and institutional approval.

Future doctor program inspires the next generation

Alongside the observership initiative, Sidra Medicine continues to grow its Future Doctor Program, which aims to inspire secondary school students interested in careers in medicine and healthcare.

Held at the hospital’s advanced Simulation Center, the five-day program provides students aged 15 to 18 with hands-on exposure to healthcare careers through simulation-based learning, mentorship sessions, clinical department visits, and interactive educational activities.

Participants receive training in first aid, emergency response, and Basic Life Support while also gaining insight into patient care and healthcare delivery.

Students can earn American Heart Association-accredited certifications, adding practical value to their learning experience.

Since its introduction, the program has helped dozens of students explore healthcare careers and make informed decisions about their academic futures.

The first session of 2026 has already concluded, with three additional sessions scheduled for later this year.

Dr. Hammad said early exposure to healthcare settings can significantly influence career choices by helping students understand the realities of medical practice and the dedication required to work in the sector.

Broader investments in healthcare education and innovation

The launch of the Medical Observership Program comes as Sidra Medicine continues to expand its role in medical education, research, and innovation.

Earlier this year, the hospital announced new family-centered healthcare initiatives, including home-based maternal and newborn care services and expanded neonatal care capabilities.

It also introduced Qatar’s first advanced gene-editing therapy for sickle cell disease and thalassemia and unveiled plans to enhance pediatric rehabilitation services through a new sensory integration gym.

In addition, Sidra Medicine recently achieved HIMSS DIAM Stage 6 validation, becoming the only healthcare organization in the Middle East and Europe to reach that level of digital imaging maturity, further reinforcing its position as a leader in healthcare innovation and medical excellence.

Through these educational initiatives, Sidra Medicine is creating opportunities for learners at every stage of their professional journey while supporting the development of a highly skilled healthcare workforce in Qatar and the wider region.

title.rendered: Tawoos Group launches Numa Health following NMC Oman acquisition

content.rendered:
[et_pb_section fb_built=”1″ _builder_version=”4.27.5″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”][et_pb_row _builder_version=”4.27.5″ _module_preset=”default” custom_margin=”6px|auto||auto||” custom_padding=”15px|||41px||” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”][et_pb_column type=”4_4″ _builder_version=”4.27.4″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”][et_pb_text _builder_version=”4.27.4″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”]

OMAN — Tawoos Group has officially launched Numa Health, a new healthcare brand that brings together the hospitals and clinics formerly operating under NMC Oman.

The move follows the successful acquisition and integration of NMC’s healthcare operations in the Sultanate, marking Tawoos Group’s entry into the private healthcare sector as it seeks to build a nationally owned healthcare platform aligned with Oman Vision 2040.

The new brand was unveiled during a private reception in Muscat attended by Oman’s Minister of Health, Dr. Hilal bin Ali Al Sabti, alongside Samir J. Fancy, Chairman of Tawoos Group, His Highness Sayyid Tarik bin Shabib Al Said, Vice Chairman of Tawoos Group, and other senior government and business leaders.

Building a national healthcare network

Tawoos Group acquired NMC Oman and Elegant Medical Center (EMC) through agreements signed in May 2025, with the transaction completed in September 2025.

Since then, the healthcare network has expanded from eight facilities to 13 locations across the Sultanate.

Under the new structure, hospitals and clinics previously operating as NMC Oman will now operate under the Numa Health brand, while EMC will continue as a dedicated sub-brand focused on dermatology and aesthetic medicine.

Together, Numa Health and EMC now form the largest private healthcare platform under Omani institutional ownership.

The network builds on more than two decades of healthcare delivery while benefiting from new governance, investment, and long-term strategic support.

The launch comes as Oman continues to prioritize healthcare development under Vision 2040.

Demand for healthcare services is rising due to population growth, an aging demographic, and increasing investment in digital health infrastructure across the country.

Recent Ministry of Health initiatives include the rollout of virtual healthcare services, AI-assisted diagnostics, and expanded telemedicine capabilities to improve access and patient outcomes.

Expanding access to advanced care

Speaking at the launch, Samir J. Fancy said the Omani government and Ministry of Health have created a strong universal healthcare system that serves the needs of a growing population.

He noted that Numa Health aims to complement those efforts by establishing a trusted Omani healthcare brand that delivers affordable, high-quality care.

He added that Tawoos plans to expand the platform’s footprint within Oman and potentially beyond its borders while introducing more advanced tertiary healthcare services.

According to Fancy, the group’s financial strength and long-term investment strategy will support Numa Health’s ambition to become a trusted private-sector healthcare partner for the country.

Focus on Patient-Centred Care

His Highness Sayyid Tarik bin Shabib Al Said said Numa Health represents more than a change in name.

He explained that the organization is shifting toward a more connected and patient-centred model of care that combines medical excellence, technology, and a human-focused approach.

He added that these principles will guide the company’s future growth and service delivery.

The launch of Numa Health follows Tawoos Group’s acquisition of NMC Oman, which included two hospitals and six clinics and aesthetic centres.

At the time of the acquisition, the company described the move as the first step toward building a sustainable private healthcare ecosystem focused on quality care, job creation, and operational excellence.

With Oman continuing to modernize its healthcare system through digital transformation, health insurance expansion, and investment in new medical infrastructure, Numa Health is positioning itself to play a larger role in meeting the country’s evolving healthcare needs.

title.rendered: Vestergaard, LifeStraw expand their malaria and safe water initiatives to protect vulnerable children in Kenya

content.rendered:
[et_pb_section fb_built=”1″ _builder_version=”4.27.5″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”][et_pb_row _builder_version=”4.27.5″ _module_preset=”default” custom_margin=”6px|auto||auto||” custom_padding=”15px|||41px||” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”][et_pb_column type=”4_4″ _builder_version=”4.27.4″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”][et_pb_text _builder_version=”4.27.4″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”]

KENYA—Global health companies Vestergaard and LifeStraw have strengthened their partnership in Kenya with a new annual commitment to donate 1,000 PermaNet® Dual long-lasting insecticidal mosquito nets to vulnerable communities in western Kenya.

The initiative builds on more than a decade of collaboration at Emusanda Health Centre in Kakamega County and supports broader efforts to improve maternal and child health through integrated malaria prevention and access to safe water.

The partnership traces its roots to 2009, when Vestergaard rehabilitated Emusanda Health Centre in Lurambi and transformed it into a community facility providing primary healthcare, maternal services, paediatric care, and HIV treatment.

Since LifeStraw became an independent company in 2020, it has continued to expand the facility by constructing a maternity ward and strengthening antenatal and postnatal services.

At the same time, Vestergaard has supplied mosquito nets to mothers delivering at the facility and to families with children under five seeking care.

According to the company, more than 6,300 PermaNet nets have already been distributed through the health centre since the programme began.

Each eligible family also receives a LifeStraw household water purifier.

In addition, LifeStraw’s local teams help bridge staffing shortages and provide essential medicines, enabling the facility to offer services around the clock.

Combining safe water and malaria prevention

The new donation programme comes as malaria continues to pose a significant public health challenge in Kenya.

While insecticide-treated mosquito nets remain one of the most effective malaria prevention tools, emerging insecticide resistance has created a need for more advanced technologies.

PermaNet Dual was developed to address this challenge by combining two active ingredients—chlorfenapyr and deltamethrin—which target mosquitoes through different modes of action.

 Studies have shown that dual-active-ingredient nets can provide greater protection in areas affected by insecticide resistance.

According to data cited by Vestergaard, insecticide-treated nets accounted for 72% of malaria cases prevented globally between 2000 and 2024, while dual-active-ingredient nets, such as PermaNet Dual, helped prevent an estimated 40 million malaria cases between 2019 and 2024.

Under the expanded partnership, the nets will be distributed not only through healthcare facilities but also to boarding schools that care for orphans and children living with disabilities, extending protection to some of the region’s most vulnerable populations.

LifeStraw’s Give Back programme has already delivered safe drinking water solutions to schools and communities across Kenya and other countries, reaching more than 14 million children.

Industry efforts intensify as malaria burden persists

The announcement comes amid renewed global efforts to combat malaria.

In April 2026, the World Health Organization (WHO) prequalified the first malaria treatment specifically designed for newborns and young infants and approved new rapid diagnostic tests capable of detecting parasite strains that evade conventional testing.

WHO estimates that malaria caused 282 million cases and approximately 610,000 deaths worldwide in 2024, highlighting the continued need for prevention and treatment innovations.

Meanwhile, Vestergaard has continued to expand its malaria prevention activities globally.

The company recently advanced plans for large-scale production of PermaNet Dual through a new manufacturing venture in Nigeria, aimed at increasing access to next-generation mosquito nets across Africa.

Commenting on the new commitment in Kenya, Amar Ali, CEO of Vestergaard, said LifeStraw’s work on the ground continues to identify critical healthcare gaps and demonstrate how targeted interventions can protect vulnerable children.

He noted that formalising the annual donation programme reinforces both companies’ commitment to helping communities access essential tools for healthier lives.

Alison Hill, CEO of LifeStraw, said access to safe water and effective malaria prevention remains fundamental to community health.

She explained that combining household water purification with next-generation mosquito nets enables the organisations to deliver complementary interventions that improve health and educational outcomes for children and families across the communities they serve.

title.rendered: Kenya’s SHA suspends M.P. Shah Hospital over billing complaints pending investigation

content.rendered:
[et_pb_section fb_built=”1″ _builder_version=”4.27.5″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”][et_pb_row _builder_version=”4.27.5″ _module_preset=”default” custom_margin=”6px|auto||auto||” custom_padding=”15px|||41px||” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”][et_pb_column type=”4_4″ _builder_version=”4.27.4″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”][et_pb_text _builder_version=”4.27.4″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”]

KENYA—M.P. Shah Hospital has been temporarily suspended from providing services to beneficiaries of the Social Health Authority (SHA) and the Social Health Insurance Fund (SHIF) following complaints related to billing practices.

The suspension, which took effect on June 23, 2026, will remain in place while SHA conducts investigations into the allegations.

The move affects services offered under the Primary Healthcare Fund (PHCF), Social Health Insurance Fund (SHIF), Emergency, Chronic and Critical Illness Fund (ECCIF), and the Public Officers Medical Scheme Fund (POMSF).

In a notice issued to beneficiaries and healthcare stakeholders, SHA Chief Executive Officer Dr. Mercy Mwangangi stated that the authority had removed the hospital from its panel of contracted healthcare providers pending the outcome of the investigations.

The authority emphasized that the action is intended to safeguard public healthcare resources and ensure accountability within the healthcare system.

Hospital responds and launches internal review

M.P. Shah Hospital acknowledged receiving the suspension notice and said it would fully cooperate with the ongoing investigations.

In a statement, the hospital said it had already initiated an internal review of its billing processes. Management also stressed that patients should not bear costs that are meant to be covered under their SHIF benefits.

The hospital noted that it takes the concerns seriously and is committed to identifying and correcting any shortcomings that may have affected patients.

It added that every patient deserves access to the healthcare services they are entitled to without facing unnecessary financial burdens.

To minimize disruptions, M.P. Shah Hospital said its teams are assisting affected patients and coordinating safe transfers to other SHA-contracted facilities where necessary.

Guidance for patients during the suspension

SHA has assured beneficiaries admitted before the suspension date that they will continue to receive treatment at M.P. Shah Hospital until the completion of their current episode of care and discharge.

However, patients seeking new admissions, follow-up treatment, outpatient services, or other healthcare services during the suspension period have been advised to seek care at alternative facilities contracted by SHA.

 Beneficiaries requiring assistance with referrals or continuity of care can access support through SHA’s established communication channels. 

Suspension comes amid wider oversight reforms

The suspension comes as the government intensifies efforts to strengthen oversight of Kenya’s healthcare financing system following the transition from the National Health Insurance Fund (NHIF) to SHA and SHIF.

In recent months, health authorities have increased scrutiny of healthcare providers over suspected fraud, overbilling, and misuse of public health insurance funds.

SHA has also introduced artificial intelligence-based monitoring systems designed to identify suspicious claims, unnecessary procedures, and irregular billing patterns.

According to reports, the technology has already flagged billions of shillings in questionable claims for further review.

The development follows earlier enforcement actions against other healthcare facilities accused of fraudulent claims practices as the authority seeks to improve transparency and accountability across the sector.

Hospital expands services despite regulatory challenge

The suspension comes just days after M.P. Shah Hospital unveiled The Hub Medical Centre in Karen, Nairobi, a new outpatient facility designed to improve access to specialised healthcare services for residents of Karen and surrounding areas.

The center is expected to provide a range of medical services closer to communities while supporting the hospital’s broader expansion strategy.

title.rendered: Thumbay Labs obtains ISO 15189:2022 to comply with current UAE CAP status

content.rendered:
[et_pb_section fb_built=”1″ _builder_version=”4.27.5″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”][et_pb_row _builder_version=”4.27.5″ _module_preset=”default” custom_margin=”6px|auto||auto||” custom_padding=”15px|||41px||” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”][et_pb_column type=”4_4″ _builder_version=”4.27.4″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”][et_pb_text _builder_version=”4.27.4″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”]

UAE—Thumbay Labs has marked 25 years of diagnostic services with a new ISO 15189:2022 accreditation, reinforcing its position as one of the region’s leading academic laboratory networks.

The certification, which focuses on quality and technical competence in medical laboratories, adds to its existing College of American Pathologists (CAP) accreditation, giving the group two globally recognised quality benchmarks.

The ISO standard evaluates the entire diagnostic process, from sample collection to reporting, ensuring laboratories consistently produce reliable results.

Together with CAP accreditation, the recognition signals strong compliance with international best practices in laboratory medicine.

From a single lab to a regional network

Thumbay Labs began in 2001 as a small diagnostic unit supporting Gulf Medical University’s clinical training and the group’s first hospital.

Over time, it expanded into a network of five laboratories across the Northern Emirates and now operates from a 25,000-square-foot facility at Thumbay Medicity.

The network supports a wider healthcare ecosystem that has served more than 19 million patients and assisted in over 100,000 births.

Over the years, it has processed an estimated 30 million laboratory tests, reflecting the scale of its clinical contribution across a highly diverse population representing more than 175 nationalities in the UAE.

High-volume testing and pandemic response

During the COVID-19 pandemic, the laboratories operated continuously as a regional molecular testing hub, processing up to 15,000 tests per day at peak demand.

This capacity strengthened its role in public health response while maintaining routine diagnostic services for hospitals and clinics across the country.

Expanding diagnostic capabilities

The laboratory group now runs multiple specialised departments, including clinical chemistry, haematology, microbiology, molecular diagnostics, histopathology, and newborn screening.

Histopathology services continue to support cancer diagnosis, while newborn screening programs help detect metabolic and genetic disorders early in infants.

In addition, the group maintains a clinical research unit and an independent quality assurance system to support its expanding operations across Thumbay Hospitals in Ajman, Dubai, and Fujairah, with plans underway for a new facility in Abu Dhabi.

Digital health and patient access

To improve accessibility, Thumbay Labs is rolling out a mobile and web application that allows patients to book and pay for tests online.

At the same time, its home sample collection service is expanding to reach more patients, including upcoming coverage in Abu Dhabi.

New frontiers in diagnostics

The laboratory is also preparing to introduce blood-based Alzheimer’s testing, which uses biomarkers such as ApoE4, pTau181, pTau217, and neurofilament light chain.

This approach aims to offer a less invasive alternative to traditional diagnostic procedures like spinal taps and PET scans.

Moving toward Lab 5.0

Looking ahead, the group is advancing a “Lab 5.0” model that integrates artificial intelligence, predictive analytics, and automation into laboratory workflows.

The approach aims to enhance early disease detection and improve diagnostic precision while maintaining consistent turnaround times and quality standards.

Across its 25-year journey, Thumbay Labs continues to position itself as a major academic diagnostic network in the region, combining large-scale testing capacity with evolving digital and research-driven healthcare solutions.

UAE—The Sheikh Khalifa Medical City—Ajman (SKMCA), overseen by The Medical Office under PureHealth, has secured Level 4 accreditation under the National Patient Safety Friendly Hospital Initiative (PSFHI).

The programme is led by the Ministry of Health and Prevention in collaboration with the World Health Organization, and it represents the highest recognition within its patient safety framework.

The accreditation followed a detailed assessment of SKMCA’s clinical operations, governance systems, and facility standards.

Evaluators examined how the hospital manages patient care across multiple departments, including safety protocols, infection control, medication handling, and continuous quality improvement processes.

Strong commitment to patient safety and clinical excellence

Level 4 status is awarded only to hospitals that demonstrate organisation-wide excellence in patient safety and healthcare delivery.

At SKMCA, the evaluation confirmed strong adherence to international standards, particularly those aligned with the PSFHI framework developed by the Ministry of Health and Prevention of the UAE, in partnership with WHO.

The hospital’s leadership emphasized that the achievement reflects long-term investment in building a safety-driven healthcare culture.

Systems for monitoring patient outcomes, reporting incidents, and improving clinical practices were highlighted as key strengths during the assessment.

Leadership response from The Medical Office and SKMCA

Dr. Aref Ali Abdulla Al Shehhi, CEO of The Medical Office, said the recognition reflects a sustained focus on global healthcare standards and patient-centred care across all facilities under its supervision.

He noted that patient safety remains a core pillar in the group’s healthcare strategy, supported by continuous training and quality assurance systems.

SKMCA CEO Mr. Khamis Al Mansoori also welcomed the accreditation, stating that it reflects the collective effort of healthcare professionals across departments.

He emphasized that the recognition confirms patients are receiving care aligned with internationally benchmarked safety and quality systems, supported by coordinated teamwork and clinical discipline.

PSFHI framework and evaluation standards

The PSFHI programme evaluates hospitals using strict criteria covering leadership commitment, clinical safety practices, patient rights, infection prevention and control, medication safety, and ongoing quality improvement.

Hospitals are required to demonstrate not only compliance but also consistency in applying safety measures across all levels of care.

Achieving Level 4 status indicates that SKMCA has met the highest threshold in the programme, reflecting maturity in its healthcare systems and operational consistency.

Continued focus on healthcare quality

SKMCA continues to strengthen its clinical governance systems and patient safety initiatives while aligning its operations with international healthcare benchmarks.

The institution remains part of broader healthcare transformation efforts led by PureHealth, which focuses on improving access, quality, and innovation in healthcare delivery across its network.

[et_pb_section fb_built=”1″ _builder_version=”4.27.5″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”][et_pb_row _builder_version=”4.27.5″ _module_preset=”default” custom_margin=”6px|auto||auto||” custom_padding=”15px|||41px||” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”][et_pb_column type=”4_4″ _builder_version=”4.27.4″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”][et_pb_text _builder_version=”4.27.4″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”]

SAUDI ARABIA—Sultan Bin Abdulaziz Humanitarian City (Sultan City), one of the largest non-profit rehabilitation and specialized healthcare facilities in the Middle East, has achieved HIMSS EMRAM Stage 7 accreditation.

This is the highest level of digital maturity for electronic medical record adoption awarded by the Healthcare Information and Management Systems Society (HIMSS).

The recognition places the 510-bed facility among a select group of healthcare institutions worldwide that operate in a fully digital and paperless clinical environment.

It reflects years of investment in health information technology, strong clinical leadership, and a commitment to improving patient care through data-driven decision-making.

HIMSS EMRAM Stage 7 is considered one of the healthcare sector’s most demanding digital maturity benchmarks.

Hospitals that attain this level demonstrate comprehensive electronic documentation, advanced analytics, strong governance structures, optimized clinical workflows, and extensive use of data to support patient safety and care quality.

The validation process includes detailed reviews of clinical workflows, system performance, and the integration of digital technologies into everyday patient care.

Building a fully integrated digital care environment

According to Sultan City, the achievement marks the culmination of a long-term digital transformation strategy that has focused on integrating clinical, operational, and administrative systems into a single connected environment.

The institution has treated more than 1.1 million patients from across the Middle East since it was established by the late Crown Prince HRH Prince Sultan Bin Abdulaziz.

Today, it provides surgical, rehabilitative, therapeutic, and supportive services through a multidisciplinary care model designed to address complex patient needs.

The Stage 7 validation confirms that Sultan City has implemented fully electronic clinical documentation, closed-loop medication management systems, advanced clinical decision support tools, and robust data analytics capabilities.

These technologies enable healthcare professionals to access accurate patient information in real time, helping them make informed decisions and coordinate care more effectively.

The hospital’s digital ecosystem is supported by a unified electronic health record platform that gives care teams a comprehensive view of patient information across clinical, administrative, and operational functions.

This approach improves communication between departments while enhancing efficiency throughout the patient journey.

Technology partnerships supporting progress

Technology partners have also contributed to the transformation.

InterSystems’ TrakCare platform supports interoperability, streamlined workflows, and real-time access to patient information through a single integrated system.

Similar digital health initiatives across Saudi Arabia continue to demonstrate how advanced electronic medical records and analytics can strengthen healthcare delivery and improve patient outcomes.

Dr. Abdullah Bin Zarah, Chief Executive Officer of Sultan City, said the achievement reflects the dedication and collaboration of teams across the organization.

“Achieving HIMSS EMRAM Stage 7 reinforces our commitment to delivering world-class, digitally enabled care and supports our ambition to continuously improve patient outcomes through innovation,” he said.

Ali Abi Raad, Managing Director for the Middle East, South Africa and India at InterSystems, said the company was proud to support Sultan City’s digital transformation journey.

“This milestone highlights the importance of collaboration and integrated technology in helping healthcare organizations achieve sustainable, high-impact progress,” he said.

Supporting Saudi Vision 2030

Sultan City noted that the achievement aligns with Saudi Vision 2030 and the Kingdom’s broader healthcare transformation agenda.

The organization plans to build on this foundation by expanding its use of predictive analytics and data-driven care models, enabling clinicians to deliver more personalized and proactive treatment.

The accreditation comes as several healthcare institutions across Saudi Arabia continue to earn advanced HIMSS recognitions, reflecting the country’s growing investment in digital health infrastructure, interoperability, and data-enabled care.

Recent Stage 7 achievements and renewals by leading Saudi healthcare organizations highlight the Kingdom’s efforts to establish a modern healthcare system that leverages technology to enhance quality, safety, and operational efficiency.

SAUDI ARABIA—Saudi Arabia’s Ministry of Health, in partnership with the National Centre for Privatisation & PPP (NCP), has awarded the contract to operate and manage the SABIC Specialised Behavioural Healthcare Hospital in North Riyadh to a consortium of Saudi and German healthcare providers.

The winning consortium, known as SEH Healthcare, brings together Tadawul-listed SMC Healthcare, German rehabilitation specialist Dr. Ebel Fachkliniken, and Saudi mental healthcare provider Health Gates Complex.

The project forms part of the Kingdom’s broader efforts to strengthen mental health services while expanding private sector participation in healthcare delivery under the Health Sector Transformation Programme.

Expanding access to specialised mental healthcare

According to NCP, the new facility will deliver a comprehensive range of behavioural and mental health services, including psychiatric care, addiction treatment, rehabilitation programmes, and long-term aftercare support.

 The project is designed to improve access to specialised treatment while enhancing the quality and efficiency of healthcare services across the Kingdom.

The hospital has a capacity of 150 beds and covers approximately 62,500 square metres.

In addition to inpatient services, the facility will house 19 outpatient clinics and six dedicated day-care rooms, enabling patients to receive treatment through a variety of care pathways.

The hospital was developed through collaboration between the Ministry of Health and the Saudi Basic Industries Corporation (SABIC), which contributed to the construction, infrastructure development, and equipping of the facility.

SMC subsidiary to lead operations

In a separate disclosure to the Saudi stock exchange, SMC Healthcare confirmed that it had received the project award letter on 17 June.

The company said its 51%-owned subsidiary, Al-Mukhtas Al-Sehhi Medical Company, will manage and operate the hospital under a 15-year public-private partnership concession agreement.

The project carries an estimated value of SAR3.8 billion (US$1.0 billion), including VAT.

Under the agreement, the consortium will oversee both clinical and non-clinical services, covering medical and non-medical operations and maintenance, facility management, equipment management, and specialised mental health and addiction treatment services.

Neither NCP nor SMC Healthcare disclosed details of the consortium’s ownership structure, project financing arrangements, or capital expenditure commitments.

Recent developments at SMC Healthcare

The award comes at a time of continued growth for SMC Healthcare.

Earlier this year, the company reported a 9.8% increase in first-quarter net profit to SAR32.55 million (US$8.68 million), supported by higher outpatient activity and growing inpatient revenues.

The company has also continued expanding its healthcare footprint in Riyadh through new outpatient facilities and has outlined plans to significantly increase its healthcare capacity over the coming years.

The SABIC Specialised Behavioural Healthcare Hospital project marks one of Saudi Arabia’s largest healthcare public-private partnerships focused on mental health services and reflects the Kingdom’s increasing emphasis on specialised care infrastructure under Vision 2030.

title.rendered: Moscow Study proves AI cannot replace human emergency radiologists

content.rendered:
[et_pb_section fb_built=”1″ _builder_version=”4.27.5″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”][et_pb_row _builder_version=”4.27.5″ _module_preset=”default” custom_margin=”6px|auto||auto||” custom_padding=”15px|||41px||” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”][et_pb_column type=”4_4″ _builder_version=”4.27.4″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”][et_pb_text _builder_version=”4.27.4″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”]

RUSSIA—Scientists in Moscow have found that the most effective way to diagnose hemorrhagic stroke from computed tomography (CT) scans is not through fully automated artificial intelligence (AI) systems, but through close collaboration between radiologists and AI tools.

The findings emerged from a large-scale study conducted by the Center for Diagnostics and Telemedicine of the Moscow Healthcare Department, which evaluated different approaches to integrating computer vision technologies into routine clinical practice.

Over a two-year period, specialists monitored the performance of three AI services and reviewed radiologists’ reports from more than 3,400 CT examinations conducted across 67 hospitals in Moscow.

The analysis showed that the best results were achieved when AI acted as a “second reader,” supporting physicians rather than replacing them.

In this model, the neural network rapidly identifies suspected bleeding sites, performs measurements, and presents preliminary findings, while the radiologist retains responsibility for the final diagnosis.

According to Yuri Vasilev, Medical Director of the Center for Diagnostics and Telemedicine, this collaborative approach significantly improves the detection of intracranial hemorrhages, including very small bleeds that can easily be overlooked.

 Early identification is particularly important because timely treatment can reduce the risk of severe complications and improve patient outcomes.

AI supports, physicians decide

The study also revealed that radiologists continue to outperform AI systems when it comes to avoiding false-positive findings.

While AI can occasionally flag abnormalities that are not actually present, physicians are better able to distinguish genuine hemorrhages from imaging artifacts or other structures.

In practice, the workflow begins immediately after a CT scan is completed. The AI system receives the images, analyzes them within minutes, highlights suspicious regions, determines the likely type of hemorrhage, and estimates its volume.

The radiologist then reviews these findings, focuses attention on the flagged areas, and makes the final clinical assessment.

This process allows clinicians to work more efficiently, particularly during emergencies when every minute counts.

Rather than replacing medical professionals, AI serves as an additional layer of support that helps physicians make faster and more informed decisions.

Expanding Moscow’s AI Healthcare Ecosystem

The Center for Diagnostics and Telemedicine continues to refine its algorithms by incorporating physician feedback, reducing false alarms, and improving performance under heavy clinical workloads.

The city’s digital radiology infrastructure connects imaging equipment across healthcare facilities, giving specialists access to advanced computer vision tools.

Moscow’s healthcare system currently uses more than 60 AI services capable of identifying diseases across 43 clinical areas.

Recent developments have further strengthened the city’s AI strategy. Earlier this month, MosMedAI launched its 18th AI-powered imaging service, designed to automatically detect and grade scoliosis from X-ray examinations.

The platform now processes more than one million imaging studies each month and supports healthcare facilities across Russia.

Moscow has also introduced new educational manuals and simulation tools to help radiologists develop practical skills in using AI safely and effectively in clinical settings.

These resources draw on years of experience gained through the city’s ongoing computer vision experiment in healthcare.

National reach through MosMedAI

Since February 2024, Moscow has expanded access to its AI technologies through the MosMedAI platform, developed by the Center for Diagnostics and Telemedicine in collaboration with the Moscow Department of Information Technology.

The platform enables regional healthcare providers to use AI services for analyzing CT scans, X-rays, mammograms, fluorograms, and other medical images.

More than 2,000 healthcare organisations across 74 Russian regions are now connected to the system, helping physicians analyse millions of studies each year.

Today, more than 2,000 healthcare organizations across 74 Russian regions use the platform, with computer vision algorithms having analyzed tens of millions of medical images nationwide.

title.rendered: Equity Afya opens flagship standalone community pharmacy in Nairobi

content.rendered:
[et_pb_section fb_built=”1″ _builder_version=”4.27.5″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}”][et_pb_row _builder_version=”4.27.5″ _module_preset=”default” custom_margin=”6px|auto||auto||” custom_padding=”15px|||41px||” global_colors_info=”{}”][et_pb_column type=”4_4″ _builder_version=”4.27.4″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}”][et_pb_text _builder_version=”4.27.4″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}”]

KENYA—Equity Afya has opened its first standalone community pharmacy at Britam Towers in Nairobi’s Upper Hill, marking a major step in the healthcare provider’s efforts to expand access to affordable medicines and primary healthcare services across Kenya and the wider region.

The new outlet serves as the flagship branch in a planned pharmacy network that will complement Equity Afya’s existing healthcare infrastructure.

The move broadens the organization’s reach beyond its 154 medical centres operating across Kenya and the Democratic Republic of Congo, many of which already house in-house pharmacies.

Expanding Access to Affordable Healthcare

The community pharmacy offers prescription and over-the-counter medicines alongside free blood pressure and blood sugar screening services.

Patients can also receive wellness and nutrition counselling and, where necessary, referrals to nearby Equity Afya clinics for further medical attention.

According to Equity Group Foundation Executive Chairman Dr. James Mwangi, the expansion reflects the Group’s commitment to improving access to quality healthcare and essential medicines.

He noted that many Kenyans still face challenges accessing licensed pharmacies, particularly in underserved areas, resulting in health inequalities and poor treatment outcomes.

To address this gap, Equity Afya plans to use a franchise model to increase the availability of quality medicines while lowering treatment costs.

Dr. Mwangi said the organization aims to reduce medicine costs by between 50% and 80%, making healthcare more affordable for households while strengthening access to safe pharmaceutical services.

Built on the Equity Leaders Program

The pharmacy initiative builds on the success of the Equity Afya model, which emerged from the Equity Group Foundation’s long-running investment in education and leadership development through the Equity Leaders Program (ELP).

Over the years, the Foundation has awarded more than 60,000 scholarships and supported over 35,000 students in securing admission to local and international universities.

Many graduates have gone on to become healthcare professionals and entrepreneurs within the Equity Afya network.

Today, Equity Afya serves an average of 130,000 patients every month and has grown into one of Africa’s largest franchised primary healthcare networks.

Gates Foundation backs expansion

The initiative has received support from the Gates Foundation, whose Regional Director for Africa, Paulin Basinga, described the partnership as an example of how private-sector expertise can address major social challenges.

He said the Foundation’s support is intended to help scale the model and facilitate expansion into rural communities across Kenya and eventually other African countries.

Equity Group Holdings Chairman Prof. Isaac Macharia revealed that the pharmacy network will be operated through a franchise system led by entrepreneurs drawn from the Equity Leaders Program.

The Group is targeting the establishment of 1,000 pharmacies over time.

Part of a broader growth strategy

The pharmacy launch comes as Equity Group continues to diversify its operations beyond banking.

In its recently released first-quarter 2026 results, the Group reported a 24% increase in profit after tax to KSh19.1 billion (US$147 million), while total assets rose to KSh2.04 trillion (US$15.7 billion).

During the same period, Equity Afya recorded more than 4.9 million cumulative patient visits through its expanding network of medical centres.

Equity Group Foundation Director of Operations Dr. Joanne Korir said the new pharmacy strengthens Equity Afya’s integrated healthcare model by linking patients to reliable medicines, preventive services and follow-up care within a trusted healthcare ecosystem.

title.rendered: Zimbabwe invests US$30M in cancer care upgrades in Mpilo and Parirenyatwa

content.rendered:
[et_pb_section fb_built=”1″ _builder_version=”4.27.5″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”][et_pb_row _builder_version=”4.27.5″ _module_preset=”default” custom_margin=”6px|auto||auto||” custom_padding=”15px|||41px||” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”][et_pb_column type=”4_4″ _builder_version=”4.27.4″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”][et_pb_text _builder_version=”4.27.4″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”]

ZIMBABWE — The Zimbabwean government has reaffirmed its commitment to strengthening cancer treatment services and modernizing healthcare infrastructure.

Finance, Economic Development and Investment Promotion Minister Professor Mthuli Ncube described healthcare spending as a strategic investment that supports economic growth while improving citizens’ wellbeing.

Speaking during a tour of Mpilo Central Hospital in Bulawayo, Prof Ncube said the government would continue investing in cancer treatment facilities, with plans already underway to expand services by acquiring specialised equipment for prostate and cervical cancer treatment.

Major Investment in Cancer Treatment

The minister inspected newly installed radiotherapy equipment at Mpilo Hospital, procured with revenue from Zimbabwe’s sugar content tax on beverages.

The government has so far invested approximately US$30 million in acquiring and installing cancer treatment equipment at Mpilo Central Hospital and Parirenyatwa Group of Hospitals.

According to Prof Ncube, the sugar tax will continue to finance future healthcare investments.

Mpilo is currently installing a low-energy radiotherapy machine designed to treat cancers located close to the skin.

Preparations are also underway for the installation of a higher-energy radiotherapy unit that has already arrived in the country.

Hospital officials expect the installation process to be completed before the end of June.

The latest upgrades follow the recent arrival of advanced multi-energy radiotherapy machines destined for Mpilo and Parirenyatwa hospitals, part of a broader government initiative to improve access to specialised cancer treatment across Zimbabwe.

Recent reports indicate that the new equipment will significantly enhance treatment precision while helping to reduce patient waiting times and longstanding treatment backlogs.

Hospital Upgrade Programme Progress

During the visit, Prof Ncube also assessed progress under the Presidential Hospital Upgrade Programme.

He expressed satisfaction with the ongoing renovations, noting that one of the refurbished hospital blocks is expected to be completed by August.

The renovations have transformed patient rooms and service areas, forming part of a nationwide effort to modernise public healthcare facilities.

The minister said the upgrades are not only improving healthcare delivery but are also creating employment opportunities, particularly for young people working on construction projects.

Reliable power for critical services

The minister also toured the hospital’s solar power installation and backup power systems. He noted that reliable electricity is essential for healthcare facilities, particularly those operating specialised diagnostic and treatment equipment.

The solar system currently supports key hospital departments, including laboratories and maternity services, while backup generators help ensure uninterrupted operations during power outages.

Expanding access to comprehensive cancer care

Prof. Ncube said the government intends to expand cancer treatment services by acquiring additional equipment for managing prostate and cervical cancer once suitable infrastructure has been constructed.

The long-term goal is to equip Mpilo and Parirenyatwa hospitals with a full range of technologies required to diagnose and treat different forms of cancer.

Recent government announcements have also highlighted plans to procure additional CT scanners, MRI scanners and other advanced diagnostic equipment to strengthen early cancer detection nationwide.

To support sustainability, the government has signed maintenance agreements with equipment suppliers and has included skills-transfer programmes to train local healthcare professionals to operate and maintain the new technology.

As newer machines become operational at major referral hospitals, older equipment will be redeployed to other institutions, helping expand cancer treatment services across Zimbabwe and bringing specialised care closer to more communities.

title.rendered: UAE MoHAP collaborates with private hospitals to improve the national emergency healthcare response system

content.rendered:
[et_pb_section fb_built=”1″ _builder_version=”4.27.5″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”][et_pb_row _builder_version=”4.27.5″ _module_preset=”default” custom_margin=”6px|auto||auto||” custom_padding=”15px|||41px||” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”][et_pb_column type=”4_4″ _builder_version=”4.27.4″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”][et_pb_text _builder_version=”4.27.4″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”]

UAE—The Ministry of Health and Prevention (MoHAP) has signed memoranda of understanding with five private healthcare providers, including Thumbay Group Hospitals, University Hospital, Ajman Hospital, Fujairah Hospital, Amina Hospital, and Dar Al Kamal Hospital.

The agreements aim to strengthen national health security and create a coordinated response system that can manage future emergencies more effectively.

 They also reinforce integration between public and private healthcare sectors to ensure continuity of services under a unified preparedness framework.

The signing ceremony was attended by Dr Amin Al Amiri, Assistant Undersecretary for the Health Regulation Sector, while the Ministry was represented by Dr Abdul Karim Abdullah Al Zarouni, Emergency Crisis and Disaster Advisor.

Emergency response and system coordination

Under the agreements, the ministry will oversee the development and regular updating of emergency response plans for participating hospitals including medical evacuation procedures and business continuity strategies.

It will also update risk registers for each facility and involve staff in simulation exercises and specialized training programs to enhance preparedness.

Participating facilities have committed to allocating up to 30% of bed capacity to the Ministry’s operations centre when required, maintaining a two-month stockpile of essential medicines and supplies, and establishing dedicated control rooms for continuous coordination.

Dr Al Zarouni said the memoranda mark a shift from general coordination to an operational partnership that unifies standards and protocols across sectors.

He added that private healthcare providers are now key partners in national health security enabling a flexible response network that can rapidly scale capacity during emergencies.

Digital integration and data management

The memoranda also emphasize digital integration through platforms such as Jahiz and Mawardna to ensure real-time data exchange and faster decision-making during crises.

They also require healthcare facilities to regularly update medical resource data and comply with national regulations on health information sharing and confidentiality.

Officials from private healthcare facilities reaffirmed their commitment to supporting the Ministry’s efforts to strengthen health security and improve emergency response coordination.

They said the collaboration enhances shared responsibility ensures business continuity and reinforces the UAE’s role in advancing global standards for healthcare preparedness.

The initiative forms part of the UAE’s broader strategy to strengthen emergency preparedness across its healthcare system, focusing on interoperability between digital platforms, rapid resource mobilisation, and coordinated hospital response structures during large-scale health incidents.

It also supports continuous training programs, simulation drills, and integration of real-time data systems to improve coordination during emergencies across all facilities nationwide.

Under the framework, participating hospitals must also maintain strict data confidentiality standards while ensuring timely reporting of critical indicators to central command centres for coordinated emergency response management systems oversight.

title.rendered: CellSave Arabia collaborates with HMS Group for UAE stem cell care

[et_pb_section fb_built=”1″ _builder_version=”4.27.5″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”][et_pb_row _builder_version=”4.27.5″ _module_preset=”default” custom_margin=”6px|auto||auto||” custom_padding=”15px|||41px||” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”][et_pb_column type=”4_4″ _builder_version=”4.27.4″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”][et_pb_text _builder_version=”4.27.4″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”]

UAE—CellSave Arabia, the largest private stem cell biobank in the GCC and part of CSG.BIO, has entered an exclusive partnership with HMS Group to expand access to advanced stem cell preservation services across its healthcare facilities in the UAE.

The collaboration integrates regenerative medicine solutions directly into maternity care pathways, strengthening options available to expectant families.

Under this agreement, CellSave Arabia will act as the exclusive provider of cord blood, cord tissue, placental tissue, cord vessel, and amnion preservation services.

The company will embed these services within HMS Group’s maternity care system, ensuring seamless coordination from pregnancy through delivery and postnatal care.

Strengthening maternal and newborn care services

According to CellSave Arabia, the partnership aims to enhance maternal and newborn healthcare standards in Dubai and beyond by making stem cell preservation more accessible within clinical settings.

The company will oversee the full process, including collection, processing, and long-term storage, while adhering to internationally recognized standards.

In particular, CellSave Arabia will follow AABB accreditation guidelines and ISO 20387 biobanking practices to maintain high levels of quality, safety, and operational consistency.

These frameworks support the reliability of stored biological materials for potential future medical use, including regenerative therapies and clinical research applications.

Leadership perspectives on the collaboration

Speaking on the agreement, Alia Abdel Razeq, Chief Operating Officer of CellSave Arabia, said the partnership represents a significant step forward in strengthening maternal healthcare services in the region.

She noted that integrating stem cell preservation into routine maternity care will help improve awareness and accessibility for families seeking advanced healthcare options.

Similarly, Mr. Alaa Attari, Chief Executive Officer of HMS Group, expressed optimism about the collaboration.

 He said the group is pleased to work with CellSave Arabia, which he described as a leader in stem cell preservation and regenerative medicine solutions.

He added that the partnership reflects HMS Group’s commitment to providing expectant parents with access to advanced healthcare tools that support long-term family well-being.

He further emphasized that both organizations aim to promote informed decision-making throughout the maternity journey.

Patient education and awareness initiatives

Beyond clinical services, the collaboration will also introduce structured patient education programs.

These will include antenatal sessions, awareness campaigns, and informational resources designed to help parents understand the value and potential applications of stem cell preservation.

By integrating education into maternity care, both organizations aim to support more informed healthcare choices.

title.rendered: PureHealth launches SAKINA for Children Mental Health Network in Abu Dhabi

content.rendered:
[et_pb_section fb_built=”1″ _builder_version=”4.27.5″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”][et_pb_row _builder_version=”4.27.5″ _module_preset=”default” custom_margin=”6px|auto||auto||” custom_padding=”15px|||41px||” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”][et_pb_column type=”4_4″ _builder_version=”4.27.4″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”][et_pb_text _builder_version=”4.27.4″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”]

UAE— PureHealth has launched SAKINA for Children, a dedicated mental health network designed to expand specialised services for children and adolescents across Abu Dhabi.

The new programme extends the existing SAKINA mental health system and focuses on improving access to integrated, child-centred care for individuals up to 18 years of age.

The initiative brings together outpatient care, early intervention services, and specialised inpatient treatment under one coordinated framework.

As a result, families can access a continuous care pathway that supports children from diagnosis through treatment and follow-up.

The launch also aligns with the UAE’s focus on strengthening family wellbeing and building resilient communities.

Comprehensive services for early diagnosis and intervention

SAKINA for Children delivers a wide range of services that address developmental, behavioural, and psychological needs.

These include child and adolescent psychiatry, developmental paediatrics, occupational therapy, speech and language therapy, behavioural interventions, and structured family psychological support.

In addition, clinicians design personalised care plans based on each child’s developmental stage and clinical condition.

This approach ensures that treatment remains tailored, responsive, and consistent with the child’s family environment.

The programme also supports early identification of conditions such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, and learning difficulties through standardised assessment tools used in global practice.

Evidence-based clinical framework and inpatient care

The care model integrates internationally recognised diagnostic frameworks such as ADOS for autism assessment, WISC for cognitive evaluation, and Conners Rating Scales for ADHD screening.

These tools help clinicians deliver accurate diagnoses while shaping targeted treatment plans.

For children requiring intensive support, SAKINA for Children offers specialised inpatient services for acute psychiatric stabilisation and neurodevelopmental care.

 These units follow strict child safety and therapeutic engagement standards, while also incorporating family participation in the treatment process.

Care teams combine psychiatric management with behavioural and psychological therapies to ensure continuity from admission to discharge.

Network expansion and multilingual accessibility

SAKINA for Children can support close to 500 children each month through its specialised programmes.

The services operate across a multilingual environment, offering care in Arabic, English, Hindi, Urdu, and Malayalam to serve Abu Dhabi’s diverse population.

The broader SAKINA network includes 34 satellite clinics, two mental health hubs, two psychiatric inpatient facilities, two neurodiversity centres, and nine integrated clinics within tertiary hospitals.

Together, these facilities strengthen access to mental health services across the emirate while supporting coordinated referrals and specialist care.

Leadership and broader healthcare integration

Her Excellency Dr Noura Khamis Al Ghaithi from the Department of Health – Abu Dhabi said the initiative reflects a commitment to early intervention and holistic child wellbeing through an integrated healthcare system.

Meanwhile, PureHealth Group CEO Shaista Asif said the programme aims to reshape how mental health services support children and families through continuity and clinical excellence.

Dr Zain Ali Al Yafai, CEO of SAKINA, added that the model focuses on integration between mental and physical healthcare while strengthening family involvement throughout the treatment journey.

Recently, PureHealth has also continued to expand its digital health capabilities and system-wide integration efforts across its hospital and specialist care platforms in the UAE healthcare sector.
